8.content: Klaleus / defold-checkpoint checkpoint Checkpoint is a library for reading from and writing to files in a Defold game engine project.

9.content: exists(path: string): boolean Whether a saved file exists. Returns a real boolean rather than the underlying file attributes, so it reads directly as a condition. Goes through lfs, so the project needs britzl/defold-lfs as a dependency. path — Path relative to project_save_path.

10.content: list(): string[] Every saved file, found by walking the save directory breadth-first. Directories are descended into rather than listed. Goes through lfs, so the project needs britzl/defold-lfs as a dependency. The file paths, relative to project_save_path.

11.content: project_save_path: string The absolute path of the project's save directory, resolved once when the module loads. Every path the other members take is relative to it, and list returns paths relative to it. Ends with a separator, e.g. /home/klaleus/.local/share/defold-checkpoint/.

12.content: project_title: string The project.title from game.project, read once when the module loads. It is the name the save directory is derived from.

13.content: read<T = unknown>(path: string): LuaMultiReturn<[ T | false, string | undefined ]> Loads a saved file. A path ending in .json is read as text and decoded with json.decode; anything else is loaded with sys.load. On success the loaded value is returned alone, so the error slot is absent; on any failure — the file missing, unreadable, or holding invalid content — the first value is false and the second is the error string. Name the saved shape through the type parameter to avoid casting at the call site. path — Path relative to project_save_path. The loaded value, or false and the error that stopped it.

14.content: write(path: string, data: unknown): LuaMultiReturn<[ boolean, string | undefined ]> Saves a value, creating any missing directories along the path first. A path ending in .json is encoded with json.encode and written as text and flushed immediately; anything else is written with sys.save. Creating the directories goes through lfs, so the project needs britzl/defold-lfs as a dependency; this corpus does not type it. path — Path relative to project_save_path. data — The value to save. true, or false and the error that stopped it.

47.content: Klaleus / defold-shutter shutter Shutter is a library for 2D camera functionality in a Defold game engine project. ShutterCamera

48.content: activate(object: Hash): Matrix4 Installs a camera's viewport, view matrix and projection matrix into the render context. Call it from a render script before drawing the world. object — The game object the camera lives on. The camera's frustum, for passing to render.draw.

49.content: camera_table: LuaMap<Hash, ShutterCamera> Every live camera, keyed by the id of the game object it lives on. The shutter.script file writes to it; read from it rather than manipulating it directly.

50.content: cancel_shake(object: Hash, parent?: boolean) Stops a running camera shake and returns the shaken object to where it started. Does nothing if no shake is running. object — The game object the camera lives on. parent — Whether the shake was started against the camera object's parent.

51.content: center_behavior: Hash Keeps the projection fixed and shrinks the viewport to preserve the display ratio, letterboxing or pillarboxing the remainder.

52.content: deactivate(): Matrix4 Restores the viewport and matrices Defold's GUI system expects, sized to the current window. Call it before drawing GUI. The frustum matching the restored matrices.

53.content: expand_behavior: Hash Keeps the viewport filling the window and widens the projection as the window grows, showing more of the game world rather than scaling it.

54.content: force_update(object: Hash) Recalculates a camera's viewport, view matrix and projection matrix immediately. The shutter.script game object already does this once per frame; call it directly only after changing a camera property mid-frame. object — The game object the camera lives on.

55.content: get_distance(object: Hash, distance: Vector3, absolute?: boolean): Vector3 Converts a screen distance into the world distance an object must travel to cover it, accounting for the camera's zoom and, under center and stretch behavior, for the viewport no longer mapping to physical screen coordinates. object — The game object the camera lives on. distance — The screen distance to convert. absolute — Skip rotating the result by the camera's rotation.

56.content: get_frustum(object: Hash): Matrix4 Returns the camera's frustum, the product of its last calculated projection and view matrices. object — The game object the camera lives on.

57.content: get_projection(object: Hash): Matrix4 Calculates the camera's orthographic projection matrix, sized from the display under center and stretch behavior and from the window under expand behavior. object — The game object the camera lives on.

58.content: get_view(object: Hash): Matrix4 Calculates the camera's view matrix from the inverse of its game object's world transform. object — The game object the camera lives on.

59.content: get_viewport(object: Hash): LuaMultiReturn<[ number, number, number, number ]> Calculates the camera's viewport in window coordinates, scaled from the game.project display size and, under center behavior, shrunk and centered to preserve the display ratio. object — The game object the camera lives on. The viewport's x, y, width and height.

60.content: screen_to_world(object: Hash, x: number, y: number, visible?: boolean): Vector3 | undefined Converts a screen position to its world position through the inverse of the camera's frustum. object — The game object the camera lives on. x — The screen position's x coordinate. y — The screen position's y coordinate. visible — Return nil instead when the position falls outside the camera's view. The world position, or nil if visible filtered it out.

61.content: shake(object: Hash, parent: boolean, count: number, duration: number, radius: number, duration_scalar?: number, radius_scalar?: number) Starts a camera shake animation, cancelling and restarting any shake already running on this camera. object — The game object the camera lives on. parent — Shake the camera object's parent instead of the camera itself. count — How many times to displace the camera before stopping. duration — Seconds each displacement takes. radius — How far each displacement moves the camera. duration_scalar — Multiplies the duration after each displacement. Defaults to 1. radius_scalar — Multiplies the radius after each displacement. Defaults to 1.

62.content: behavior: Hash One of center_behavior, expand_behavior or stretch_behavior.

66.content: shake_origin?: Vector3 Where the shaken object sat before the shake began, and nil while no shake is running. cancel_shake restores the object to it.

72.content: viewport_x_adjusted: number Viewport left edge after the window scale and any letterboxing margin.

74.content: viewport_y_adjusted: number Viewport bottom edge after the window scale and any pillarboxing margin.

77.content: stretch_behavior: Hash Keeps both the viewport and the projection filling the window, so the game world distorts with the window ratio.

78.content: world_to_screen(object: Hash, position: Vector3, visible?: boolean): Vector3 | undefined Converts a world position to its screen position through the camera's frustum. object — The game object the camera lives on. position — The world position to convert. visible — Return nil instead when the position falls outside the camera's view. The screen position, or nil if visible filtered it out.

93.content: 8bitskull / dicebag dicebag Dicebag is a Defold extension containing probability functions designed specifically for games.

94.content: bag_create(id: string | number | Hash, num_success: number, num_fails: number, reset_on_success: boolean) Create a marble bag of green (success) and red (fails) 'marbles'. This allows you to, for example, make an unlikely event more and more likely the more fails are accumulated. id — A unique identifier for the marble bag. num_success — The number of success marbles in the bag. num_fails — The number of fails marbles in the bag. reset_on_success — Whether or not the bag should reset when a successful result is drawn. If false or nil the bag will reset when all marbles have been drawn.

95.content: bag_draw(id: string | number | Hash): boolean Draw a marble from a previously created bag. id — A unique identifier for the marble bag. True or false

96.content: bag_reset(id: string | number | Hash) Manually reset a marble bag. Will also be called when a marble bag is empty, or a success is drawn in a bag where reset_on_success is true. id — A unique identifier for the marble bag.

97.content: bags: LuaMap<string | number | Hash, { success: number; fail: number; full_success: number; full_fail: number; reset_on_success: boolean; }> Every marble bag bag_create has made, keyed by its identifier. bag_draw reads and decrements the counts here; bag_reset restores them from the full pair.

98.content: flip_coin(): boolean Flip a coin. true or false (50% chance).

99.content: roll_custom_dice(num_dice: number, sides: Array<[ number, number ]>): number Roll custom dice. The dice can have sides with different weights and different values. num_dice — How many dice to roll. sides — A table describing the sides of the die in the format [[weight1, value1], [weight2, value2], ...]. The sum of the values as specified in the table sides.

100.content: roll_dice(num_dice: number, num_sides: number, modifier: number): number Roll a number of dice, D&D-style. An example would be rolling 3d6+2. Returns the sum of the resulting roll. num_dice — Number of dice to roll. num_sides — Number of sides on the dice. modifier — Number to add to the result. Sum of rolled dice plus modifier.

101.content: roll_special_dice(num_sides: number, advantage: number, num_dice: number, num_results: number): number Roll a number of dice and choose one (or more) of the highest (advantage) or lowest (disadvantage) results. Returns the sum of the relevant dice rolls. num_sides — Number of sides on the dice. advantage — If true, the highest rolls will be selected, otherwise the lowest values will be selected. num_dice — Number of dice to roll. num_results — How many of the highest (advantage) or lowest (disadvantage) dice to sum up. Sum of the highest (advantage) or lowest (disadvantage) dice rolls

102.content: set_up_rng(seed?: number): number Sets up the randomseed and clears the first number of random rolls. seed — optional seed, if not specified a seed will be generated using socket.gettime(). the number used to seed the random function.

103.content: table_create(id: string | number | Hash, rollable_table: Array<[ number, any, boolean? ]>) Create a rollable table. This is similar to a marble bag, except each entry can have a different weight, and can return any value (not just a boolean). id — A unique identifier for the rollable table. rollable_table — A table of weights, values and reset flags.

104.content: table_reset(id: string | number | Hash) Manually reset a rollable table. Will also be called when the rollable table is empty, or a drawn value where reset_on_roll is true. id — A unique identifier for the rollable table.

105.content: table_roll(id: string | number | Hash): any Draw a random value from the rollable table created in table_create. The value will be removed from the table. If reset_on_roll is true, the table will reset. Otherwise, the table will reset when all values are drawn. id — A unique identifier for the rollable table. The value specified in table_create.

106.content: tables: LuaMap<string | number | Hash, { active: Array<[ number, any, boolean? ]>; original: Array<[ number, any, boolean? ]>; }> Every rollable table table_create has made, keyed by its identifier. active is what table_roll draws from and removes as it goes; original is the untouched copy table_reset restores from.

127.content: abadonna / defold-detour detour Recast/Detour navigation meshes: path queries and crowd agents. NavMesh PathPoint Crowd CrowdAgent

128.content: add_agent(position: Vector3, radius: number, height: number, max_acceleration: number, max_speed: number, update_flags: number): number Adds an agent at a position on the mesh. position — Where the agent starts. radius — Radius of the agent. height — Height of the agent. max_acceleration — Largest change of velocity per second. max_speed — Largest speed. update_flags — Detour dtUpdateFlags to steer with: 1 anticipate turns, 2 avoid obstacles, 4 keep apart from other agents, 8 optimize the path by visibility, 16 optimize the path by topology. The agent id, or -1 when the crowd already holds 128 agents. 0️⃣ 0-based; passed to detour unchanged.

129.content: position: Vector3 Where the agent is after the update.

130.content: state: "walk" | "offmesh" | "invalid" "walk" on the mesh, "offmesh" on an off-mesh connection, else "invalid".

131.content: velocity: Vector3 The agent's velocity after the update.

132.content: remove_agent(agent: number) Removes an agent from the crowd. agent — Id of the agent, as {@link Crowd.add_agent} returned it. 0️⃣ 0-based; passed to detour unchanged.

133.content: reset_target(agent?: number) Stops agents moving toward their target. agent — Id of the agent to stop. When omitted, every agent is stopped. 0️⃣ 0-based; passed to detour unchanged.

134.content: set_target(target: Vector3, agent?: number) Sends agents toward the point of the mesh nearest to target. target — Where to go. agent — Id of the agent to send. When omitted, every active agent is sent. 0️⃣ 0-based; passed to detour unchanged.

135.content: update(dt: number): LuaTable<number, CrowdAgent> Moves every agent by one step of the simulation. dt — Time step in seconds. The active agents, keyed by agent id. Read them with get or pairs: keys start at 0 and skip inactive agents, so this is not an array. 0️⃣ 0-based; passed to detour unchanged.

136.content: init(navmesh: string): NavMesh Loads a navigation mesh. navmesh — The bytes of a Recast navmesh set file, such as sys.load_resource returns. The mesh.

137.content: create_crowd(max_agent_radius: number): Crowd Prepares the mesh's crowd for up to 128 agents. Calling it again resets the same crowd. max_agent_radius — Radius of the largest agent the crowd will hold. The crowd.

138.content: delete() Frees the mesh and its crowd. Neither can be used after it.

139.content: find_path(start: Vector3, finish: Vector3, straight_path_options?: number): LuaTable<number, PathPoint> Finds a path between the points of the mesh nearest to start and finish. When finish cannot be reached, the path ends at the reachable point nearest to it; when no path is found, the table is empty. start — Where to start from. finish — Where to go. straight_path_options — Detour dtStraightPathOptions: 1 adds a corner where the path crosses into another area, 2 where it crosses any polygon edge. Default is 0. The corners of the path, in order. Read them with get or pairs: keys start at 0, so this is not an array. 0️⃣ 0-based; passed to detour unchanged.

140.content: set_area_cost(costs: number[]) Sets the cost of crossing each area. The defaults are 1 for areas 0, 2 and 3, 10 for area 1, 2 for area 4 and 1.5 for area 5. costs — Cost per area: costs[0] is the cost of area 0.

141.content: set_include_flags(flags: number) Sets the polygon flags a path may cross. The default is every flag but 0x10, which marks disabled polygons. flags — Bit mask of polygon flags.

142.content: area: number Area id of the polygon the corner lies on.

143.content: end?: true true on the corner the path ends at.

144.content: offmesh?: true true on a corner that starts an off-mesh connection.

145.content: position: Vector3 Where the corner lies on the mesh.

146.content: start?: true true on the corner the path starts from.

171.content: abadonna / defold-ink ink The Ink language runtime implementation in Lua, an alternative to Narrator, based on parsing ink JSON files. Story Paragraph Answer StoryState SerializedStory

172.content: tags: string[] The tags attached to the choice, empty when it has none.

174.content: create(s: string): Story Parses a compiled ink story and returns a story instance. s — The ink JSON text, for example from sys.load_resource. It must be UTF-8. The story instance.

175.content: tags: string[] The tags attached to the paragraph, empty when it has none.

176.content: text: string The paragraph text, trimmed. It is empty for a paragraph that only carries tags.

177.content: globals: LuaTable<string, unknown> The story's global variables.

178.content: root: LuaTable The visit counts of the story's containers.

179.content: add_observer: (name: string, f: (this: void, value: unknown) => void) => void Assigns an observer function to a global variable. Each global variable can have multiple observers.

180.content: assign_value: (name: string, value: unknown) => void Assigns a value to a global variable and calls all its observers.

181.content: bind: (name: string, f: (this: void, ...args: any[]) => unknown) => void Binds a Lua function to an ink external function, which the story then calls with the external function's arguments.

182.content: continue: (answer?: number) => StoryOutput Returns the next paragraphs and choices.

183.content: deserialize: (data: SerializedStory, path: string, reset_observers?: boolean) => StoryOutput Restores the story's variables and visit counts from serialize, then jumps to a path and returns its paragraphs and choices.

184.content: eval: (expression: string) => unknown Returns the result of evaluating a Lua expression, with the name of every global variable replaced by its value.

185.content: get_state: () => StoryState Returns the current state of the story, to save and pass to restore later.

186.content: jump: (path: string) => StoryOutput Jumps to a named knot or stitch, and returns its paragraphs and choices.

187.content: remove_observer: (name: string, f?: (this: void, value: unknown) => void) => void Removes an observer function.

188.content: restore: (state: StoryState, with_bindings?: boolean, ignore_errors?: boolean) => StoryOutput Restores the story from a state saved with get_state, by replaying it from the start, and returns its last paragraphs and choices. The story should be created from the same, or a similar, JSON.

189.content: serialize: () => SerializedStory Returns the story's variables and visit counts, an alternative to get_state that survives script changes better. Pass it to deserialize, not to restore.

190.content: input: LuaTable[] The player's inputs, in order: answers, jumps, flow switches and assigned values.

191.content: randoms: number[] The random values the story rolled, so a replay rolls the same ones.

192.content: switch_flow: (name?: string) => void Creates a new parallel flow or switches to an existing one.

193.content: variables: LuaTable<string, unknown> A table of all global variables, to read and set. Use assign_value to notify observer functions about a change.

194.content: StoryOutput type StoryOutput = LuaMultiReturn<[ Paragraph[], Answer[] ]>

362.content: alfowler1976 / defold_browser_io browser_io Callback-based browser clipboard and file I/O for Defold. Browser operations are available on HTML5 builds; capability functions report support in the current browser.

363.content: browser_io.can_copy(): boolean Returns true when clipboard text writing is available in the current browser context. supported — True when browser_io.copy can be attempted.

364.content: browser_io.can_drop_files(): boolean Returns true when the browser exposes drag-and-drop and file-reading APIs. This does not guarantee that external file dropping is practical on touch-only devices. supported — True when drag-and-drop APIs are available.

365.content: browser_io.can_open_file(): boolean Returns true when the browser exposes the APIs required to open and read a file. supported — True when browser_io.open_file can be attempted.

366.content: browser_io.can_paste(): boolean Returns true when clipboard text reading is available in the current browser context. Browser permission or user-gesture rules can still reject an individual request. supported — True when browser_io.paste can be attempted.

367.content: browser_io.can_save_file(): boolean Returns true when the browser exposes the APIs required to create a downloadable file. supported — True when browser_io.save_file can be attempted.

368.content: browser_io.cancel_drop_listener() Removes the persistent drag-and-drop listener and releases its Lua callback.

369.content: browser_io.copy(text: string, callback: function): number Copies UTF-8 text to the browser clipboard asynchronously. Call from a direct user interaction where required by the browser. text — Text to copy. callback — Called as callback(self, result). result contains success, cancelled, operation, and error when applicable. request_id — Request identifier.

370.content: browser_io.is_supported(): boolean Returns true when the extension is running on an HTML5 build. This is a platform check; use can functions for individual browser capabilities. supported — True on HTML5, false on other platforms.

371.content: browser_io.open_file(callback: function): number Opens the browser file picker and asynchronously reads one file. Supported forms are open_file(callback), open_file(nil, callback), and open_file(options, callback). callback — Called as callback(self, result). On success result.name, result.data, and result.size are set. Empty files return data as an empty string and size as 0. request_id — Request identifier. browser_io.open_file(options: table | undefined, callback: function): number Opens the browser file picker and asynchronously reads one file. Supported forms are open_file(callback), open_file(nil, callback), and open_file(options, callback). options — Optional table. accept is an HTML accept string and max_size is the maximum file size in bytes. The default max_size is 16 MiB. callback — Called as callback(self, result). On success result.name, result.data, and result.size are set. Empty files return data as an empty string and size as 0. request_id — Request identifier.

372.content: browser_io.paste(callback: function): number Reads UTF-8 text from the browser clipboard asynchronously. Call from a direct user interaction where required by the browser. callback — Called as callback(self, result). On success result.data contains the clipboard text and result.size contains its byte length. request_id — Request identifier.

373.content: browser_io.save_file(filename: string, data: string, callback: function): number Creates a browser download from a Lua string. Binary strings are supported. Supported forms are save_file(filename, data, callback), save_file(filename, data, nil, callback), and save_file(filename, data, options, callback). filename — Suggested downloaded filename. data — File bytes. callback — Called as callback(self, result) when the download has been handed to the browser. request_id — Request identifier. browser_io.save_file(filename: string, data: string, options: table | undefined, callback: function): number Creates a browser download from a Lua string. Binary strings are supported. Supported forms are save_file(filename, data, callback), save_file(filename, data, nil, callback), and save_file(filename, data, options, callback). filename — Suggested downloaded filename. data — File bytes. options — Optional table. mime_type defaults to application/octet-stream. callback — Called as callback(self, result) when the download has been handed to the browser. request_id — Request identifier.

374.content: browser_io.set_drop_listener(callback: function): boolean Registers a persistent file drag-and-drop listener on the browser window. Supported forms are set_drop_listener(callback), set_drop_listener(nil, callback), and set_drop_listener(options, callback). callback — Called for each completed drop as callback(self, result). On success result.name, result.data, and result.size are set. enabled — True when the listener was enabled on HTML5, false on unsupported build targets. browser_io.set_drop_listener(options: table | undefined, callback: function): boolean Registers a persistent file drag-and-drop listener on the browser window. Supported forms are set_drop_listener(callback), set_drop_listener(nil, callback), and set_drop_listener(options, callback). options — Optional table. accept filters dropped files and max_size limits the number of bytes read. The default max_size is 16 MiB. callback — Called for each completed drop as callback(self, result). On success result.name, result.data, and result.size are set. enabled — True when the listener was enabled on HTML5, false on unsupported build targets.

521.content: astrochili / defold-illumination illumination Forward shading lighting for 3D games, with ambient and directional light, point and spot lights, and linear or radial fog. Add illumination.go to the scene as the sunlight source, add light_point.go or light_spot.go for each light, and set /illumination/materials/model.material on the meshes. The lighting data reaches the shader as a texture, so no render script is needed. The module's functions toggle the debug meshes and set lights and the environment by hand. Environment Light

522.content: ambient_color?: Vector4 The ambient light color, its w the ambient strength.

523.content: fog_color?: Vector4 The fog color, its w the fog's full strength. Also posted as clear_color to @render:.

524.content: fog_max?: number The distance at which the fog reaches full strength. Values below fog_min are raised to it.

525.content: fog_min?: number The distance at which the fog begins. Values below 0 are raised to 0.

526.content: fog_type?: FogType The fog type. The fog fields below apply only while the fog type is not FOG_TYPE_NONE.

527.content: sunlight_color?: Vector4 The directional light color, its w the sunlight brightness.

528.content: sunlight_direction?: Vector3 The direction the sunlight shines, normalized by upstream.

529.content: sunlight_specular?: number The sunlight's specular component, from 0 to 1.

530.content: FOG_TYPE_LINEAR: 1 Fog along the camera's view direction.

532.content: FOG_TYPE_RADIAL: 2 Fog around the camera's position.

533.content: is_debug(): boolean Returns whether the debug meshes show.

534.content: color: Vector4 The light color, multiplied with the diffuse color. Its w is the brightness.

535.content: cutoff: number The spotlight cutoff, from 0 to 1: 0.3 is like a flashlight, 0.5 half of the sphere, and 1 no cutoff.

536.content: direction?: Vector3 The direction a spotlight shines. Read only while cutoff is below 1.

537.content: position: Vector3 The light's world position. Each axis is encoded within -2048 to 2048.

538.content: radius: number The light radius. Upstream rounds it up and caps it at 255.

539.content: smoothness?: number The light's attenuation, from 0 to 1: 0 fills the radius evenly and 1 fades from the center to the edge. Defaults to 1.

540.content: specular?: number The light's specular component, from 0 to 1. Defaults to 1.

541.content: set_debug(is_enabled: boolean) Shows or hides the debug meshes of the sun and the light sources. is_enabled — Whether the debug meshes show.

542.content: set_environment(environment: Environment) Patches the environment with the fields given and leaves the others as they are. The fog fields apply only while the stored fog type, including one set in the same call, is not FOG_TYPE_NONE, and fog_color also posts clear_color to @render:. The bundled illumination.go patches each field from its own properties on its first update and whenever that property changes, overwriting a value set here. Raises until the bundled illumination.go has run its script's init. environment — The fields to change.

543.content: set_light(light: Light | undefined, url: Url | string | Hash) Adds, updates or removes a light source by hand, for lights that are not light_point.go or light_spot.go. position, color, radius and cutoff are required, specular and smoothness default to 1, and each position axis must lie within -2048 to 2048. undefined, or a light whose color.w, radius or cutoff is 0 or below, removes the light. url keys the light, so pass the same value on every call for the same light. It receives a debug message carrying is_enabled when the light is added or removed and on every set_debug. Adding or updating a light raises until the bundled illumination.go has run its script's init. light — The light, or undefined to remove it. url — The light's key and the address of its debug messages.

544.content: FogType type FogType = typeof FOG_TYPE_NONE | typeof FOG_TYPE_LINEAR | typeof FOG_TYPE_RADIAL

552.content: astrochili / defold-operator · bezier operator.bezier Linear, quadratic and cubic bezier curves through vector or number points, with a uniform position along the curve's length. The Operator camera moves along these curves, and a project can use them for its own paths.

554.content: position(time: number): P Returns the classic position along the curve at a progress. time is not clamped, so a value outside 0 to 1 extrapolates. time — The progress, from 0 to 1.

555.content: uniform_position(time: number): P Returns the uniform position along the curve: the point at that fraction of the curve's length. time is clamped between 0 and 1, and the accuracy depends on the samples_count given to new. time — The progress, from 0 to 1.

556.content:
new

(points: P[], samples_count?: number, length_func?: (v: P) => number, lerp_func?: (t: number, a: P, b: P) => P): Bezier

Creates a bezier instance from 2 to 4 points: 2 give a straight line, 3 a quadratic curve and 4 a cubic curve. Any other count fails an assert. The default length function is vmath.length, which rejects numbers, so number points need a length_func such as math.abs. points — The points, from the start of the curve to its end. samples_count — The number of segments uniform_position measures the curve with, a whole number. It defaults to 1, and 2 points always use 1. length_func — Returns the length of the difference of two points. Defaults to vmath.length. lerp_func — Interpolates between two points. Defaults to vmath.lerp. new(points: number[], samples_count: number | undefined, length_func: (v: number) => number, lerp_func?: (t: number, a: number, b: number) => number): Bezier Creates a bezier instance from 2 to 4 number points: 2 give a straight line, 3 a quadratic curve and 4 a cubic curve. Any other count fails an assert. It defaults to 1, and 2 points always use 1. length_func — Returns the length of the difference of two points. lerp_func — Interpolates between two points. Defaults to vmath.lerp.

581.content: astrochili / defold-operator · operator operator.operator Shared settings and math helpers for the Operator camera controller. The camera itself is driven by the properties and messages of operator/operator/operator.script (activate, follow_point, manual_control and the rest), which are not members of this module. The settings fields are plain module fields; assigning one goes through a cast, since a namespace import is read-only: (operator as { flight_look_easing: (this: void, x: number) => number }).flight_look_easing = (x) => x.

582.content: angle_between(v1: Vector3, v2: Vector3): number Returns the angle between two vectors, in degrees from 0 to 180. A vector of zero length gives NaN. v1 — The first vector. v2 — The second vector.

583.content: camera_collisions_groups: Hash[] The collision groups tested by the raycast from the operator anchor to the camera, so the camera stays in front of obstacles. Read on every raycast. Starts as [hash("default")].

584.content: clamp_angle(angle: number, min: number, max: number): number Brings an angle beyond 360 or -360 degrees back by one full turn, then clamps it between min and max. angle — The angle, in degrees. min — The smallest angle returned, in degrees. max — The largest angle returned, in degrees.

585.content: EASING_INOUT_CIRC(x: number): number Circular ease-in-out: maps a progress from 0 to 1 to an eased progress from 0 to 1. x — The progress, from 0 to 1.

586.content: EASING_INOUT_CUBIC(x: number): number Cubic ease-in-out: maps a progress from 0 to 1 to an eased progress from 0 to 1. x — The progress, from 0 to 1.

587.content: EASING_INOUT_EXPO(x: number): number Exponential ease-in-out: maps a progress from 0 to 1 to an eased progress from 0 to 1. x — The progress, from 0 to 1.

588.content: EASING_INOUT_QUAD(x: number): number Quadratic ease-in-out: maps a progress from 0 to 1 to an eased progress from 0 to 1. It is the default flight_look_easing. x — The progress, from 0 to 1.

589.content: EASING_INOUT_QUART(x: number): number Quartic ease-in-out: maps a progress from 0 to 1 to an eased progress from 0 to 1. x — The progress, from 0 to 1.

590.content: EASING_INOUT_QUINT(x: number): number Quintic ease-in-out: maps a progress from 0 to 1 to an eased progress from 0 to 1. x — The progress, from 0 to 1.

591.content: EASING_INOUT_SINE(x: number): number Sine ease-in-out: maps a progress from 0 to 1 to an eased progress from 0 to 1. x — The progress, from 0 to 1.

592.content: euler_from_quat(quat: Quaternion): Vector3 Converts a rotation to Euler angles in degrees, about the x, y and z axes. It reads them back in the order y x z, so it reverses quat_from_euler when the z angle is 0. At an x angle near 90 or -90 degrees the z angle is 0. quat — The rotation.

593.content: flight_bezier_samples_count: number The number of bezier segments an operator samples a flight path with, which sets how accurate its uniform position is. Read each time an operator starts flying to the next motion point. 16 is usually enough; starts at 32.

594.content: flight_look_easing: (x: number) => number The easing function that turns the camera between motion points, taking the progress from 0 to 1 and returning the eased progress. Starts as EASING_INOUT_QUAD; any of the EASING_INOUT functions, or a project's own, can replace it.

595.content: get_active_operator(): Url | undefined Returns the url of the active operator's game object, or undefined when no operator is active.

596.content: is_debug(): boolean Returns whether debug mode is on. Starts false.

597.content: lerp(t: number, a: number, b: number): number Linearly interpolates from a to b, returning a + (b - a) t. t is not clamped, so a value outside 0 to 1 extrapolates. t — The progress, 0 giving a and 1 giving b. a — The start value. b — The end value. lerp(t: number, a: Vector3, b: Vector3): Vector3 Linearly interpolates from vector a to vector b, returning a + (b - a) t as a new vector. t is not clamped, so a value outside 0 to 1 extrapolates. t — The progress, 0 giving a and 1 giving b. a — The start vector. b — The end vector.

598.content: normalized_target_angle(original: number, target: number): number Returns target, shifted by one full turn when that makes the turn from original no more than 180 degrees, so an animation from original takes the short way round. original — The current angle, in degrees. target — The wanted angle, in degrees.

599.content: normalized_target_euler(original: Vector3, target: Vector3): Vector3 Applies normalized_target_angle to each of the x, y and z angles, returning a new vector. original — The current Euler angles, in degrees. target — The wanted Euler angles, in degrees.

600.content: project_on_plane(plane_normal: Vector3, v: Vector3): Vector3 Projects a vector onto the plane through the origin with the given normal, returning v - plane_normal vmath.dot(plane_normal, v). The normal must have unit length for the result to lie on the plane. plane_normal — The plane's normal, of unit length. v — The vector to project.

601.content: quat_from_euler(euler: Vector3): Quaternion Converts Euler angles in degrees to a rotation, composed as z y x from the rotations about each axis. euler — The angles about the x, y and z axes, in degrees.

602.content: set_debug(is_debug: boolean) Turns debug mode on or off for every operator and checkpoint: on, they show their camera and checkpoint meshes and draw the active bezier path. is_debug — true to turn debug mode on.

Both buffers must carry a uint8 rgb stream of three or four components per pixel and hold at least width height elements. 2568.content: britzl / defold-png png Encode raw pixels into PNG bytes and decode PNG bytes into a Defold buffer, powered by LodePNG.

2569.content: decode_rgba(png: string, premultiply_alpha?: boolean): LuaMultiReturn<[ Opaque<"buffer"> & { length: LuaLengthMethod<number>; }, number, number ] | [ undefined, undefined, undefined ]> Decodes a valid PNG into an RGBA buffer with one uint8 pixels stream of four components per pixel. The decoded rows are flipped vertically to match Defold's buffer orientation. The extension ignores LodePNG's decode error, so a corrupt PNG may crash the engine instead of returning nils. Three nils mean the buffer could not be created or failed validation, so check the buffer before reading the dimensions. png — The PNG bytes, which must be a valid PNG. premultiply_alpha — Multiply each pixel's color components by its alpha while decoding. The pixel buffer, its width and its height, or three nils when the buffer cannot be created or fails validation.

2570.content: decode_rgb(png: string, premultiply_alpha?: boolean): LuaMultiReturn<[ Opaque<"buffer"> & { length: LuaLengthMethod<number>; }, number, number ] | [ undefined, undefined, undefined ]> Decodes a valid PNG into an RGB buffer with one uint8 pixels stream of three components per pixel. The decoded rows are flipped vertically to match Defold's buffer orientation. The extension ignores LodePNG's decode error, so a corrupt PNG may crash the engine instead of returning nils. Three nils mean the buffer could not be created or failed validation, so check the buffer before reading the dimensions. png — The PNG bytes, which must be a valid PNG. premultiply_alpha — Accepted for symmetry with {@link png.decode_rgba}; it only has effect in the RGBA path. The pixel buffer, its width and its height, or three nils when the buffer cannot be created or fails validation.

2572.content: encode_rgb(pixels: string, width: number, height: number): string Encodes raw RGB pixels (3 bytes per pixel) into PNG bytes. pixels — The raw pixel data, row by row. width — Width of the image in pixels. height — Height of the image in pixels. The PNG bytes.

5186.content: facebook.login_with_permissions(permissions: table, audience: number, callback: function) Login to Facebook and request a set of publish permissions. The user is prompted to authorize the application using the login dialog of the specific platform. Even if the user is already logged in to Facebook this function can still be used to request additional publish permissions. A comprehensive list of permissions can be found in the Facebook permissions documentation, as well as in their guide to best practices for login management. Log in to Facebook with a set of publish permissions Log in to Facebook with a set of read permissions permissions — table with the requested publish permission strings. audience — The audience that should be able to see the publications. Can be any of facebook.AUDIENCE_NONE facebook.AUDIENCE_ONLYME facebook.AUDIENCE_FRIENDS facebook.AUDIENCE_EVERYONE callback — Callback function that is executed when the permission request dialog is closed.

5187.content: facebook.login_with_tracking_preference(login_tracking: number, permissions: table, crypto_nonce: string, callback: function) iOS ONLY. Login to Facebook and request a set of permissions. Allows developers to signal that a login is limited in terms of tracking users. The user is prompted to authorize the application using the login dialog of the specific platform. Even if the user is already logged in to Facebook this function can still be used to request additional publish permissions. A comprehensive list of permissions can be found in the Facebook permissions documentation, as well as in their guide to best practices for login management. For Limited Login the list of permissions can be found in the Permissions in Limited Login documentation. Log in to Facebook with a set of publish permissions Log in to Facebook with a set of read permissions login_tracking — The tracking type for the login. Can be any of facebook.LOGIN_TRACKING_LIMITED facebook.LOGIN_TRACKING_ENABLED permissions — table with the requested publish permission strings. crypto_nonce — Nonce that the configuration was created with. A unique nonce will be used if none is provided to the factory method. callback — Callback function that is executed when the permission request dialog is closed.

5202.content: facebook.post_event(event: number | string, value: number, params?: table) Post an event to Facebook Analytics This function will post an event to Facebook Analytics where it can be used in the Facebook Insights system. Post a spent credits event to Facebook Analytics event — An event can either be one of the predefined constants below or a text string which can be used to define a custom event that is registered with Facebook Analytics. facebook.EVENT_ACHIEVED_LEVEL - facebook.EVENT_ADDED_PAYMENT_INFO - facebook.EVENT_ADDED_TO_CART - facebook.EVENT_ADDED_TO_WISHLIST - facebook.EVENT_COMPLETED_REGISTRATION - facebook.EVENT_COMPLETED_TUTORIAL - facebook.EVENT_INITIATED_CHECKOUT - facebook.EVENT_PURCHASED - facebook.EVENT_RATED - facebook.EVENT_SEARCHED - facebook.EVENT_SPENT_CREDITS - facebook.EVENT_TIME_BETWEEN_SESSIONS - facebook.EVENT_UNLOCKED_ACHIEVEMENT - facebook.EVENT_VIEWED_CONTENT value — A numeric value for the event. This should represent the value of the event, such as the level achieved, price for an item or number of orcs killed. params — Optional table with parameters and their values. A key in the table can either be one of the predefined constants below or a text which can be used to define a custom parameter. facebook.PARAM_CONTENT_ID - facebook.PARAM_CONTENT_TYPE - facebook.PARAM_CURRENCY - facebook.PARAM_DESCRIPTION - facebook.PARAM_LEVEL - facebook.PARAM_MAX_RATING_VALUE - facebook.PARAM_NUM_ITEMS - facebook.PARAM_PAYMENT_INFO_AVAILABLE - facebook.PARAM_REGISTRATION_METHOD - facebook.PARAM_SEARCH_STRING - facebook.PARAM_SOURCE_APPLICATION - facebook.PARAM_SUCCESS

5204.content: facebook.show_dialog(dialog: string, param: table, callback: function) Show facebook web dialog Display a Facebook web dialog of the type specified in the dialog parameter. The param table should be set up according to the requirements of each dialog type. Note that some parameters are mandatory. Below is the list of available dialogs and where to find Facebook's developer documentation on parameters and response data. "apprequests" Shows a Game Request dialog. Game Requests allows players to invite their friends to play a game. Available parameters [type:string] title [type:string] message [type:number] action_type [type:number] filters [type:string] data [type:string] object_id [type:table] suggestions [type:table] recipients [type:string] to On success, the "result" table parameter passed to the callback function will include the following fields [type:string] request_id [type:table] to Details for each parameter "feed" The Feed Dialog allows people to publish individual stories to their timeline. [type:string] caption [type:string] description [type:string] picture [type:string] link [type:table] people_ids [type:string] place_id [type:string] ref On success, the "result" table parameter passed to the callback function will include the following fields [type:string] post_id Details for each parameter "appinvite" The App Invite dialog is available only on iOS and Android. Note that the url parameter corresponds to the appLinkURL (iOS) and setAppLinkUrl (Android) properties. [type:string] url [type:string] preview_image Details for each parameter Show a dialog allowing the user to share a post to their timeline dialog — Dialog to show "apprequests" "feed" "appinvite" param — table with dialog parameters callback — Callback function that is called when the dialog is closed.

5618.content: gpgs.achievement_get() Get information about all achievement's state asynchronously. Result return to callback previously set by gpgs.set_callback with message_id == gpgs.MSG_GET_ACHIEVEMENTS. Result is an array of JSON strings. Decode each string with json.decode() to get a table containing the following fields id - achievement id (from GP console) name - achievement name description - achievement description xp - how much experience points will be added when achievement will be unlocked steps - current step of incremental achievement total_steps - total amount of steps of incremental achievement unlocked - set to true if achievement is unlocked. 6731.content: defold / extension-levelplay levelplay Functions and constants for Unity LevelPlay mediation on Android and iOS.

6739.content: levelplay.create_banner_ad(ad_unit_id: string, options?: table): number Creates a reusable banner ad view after successful initialization. Its ad-unit ID and all options are fixed for the view's lifetime. Create it once, then load, hide, show, and auto-refresh the same handle until it is permanently destroyed. ad_unit_id — Banner ad-unit ID from the LevelPlay dashboard. options — Creation-time banner configuration. These fields apply to every load and show; changing one requires destroying the handle and creating a new banner. handle — Positive handle, or nil when native creation is rejected.

6740.content: levelplay.create_interstitial_ad(ad_unit_id: string, bid_floor?: number): number Creates a reusable interstitial ad object after successful initialization. Its ad-unit ID and optional bid floor are fixed for the object's lifetime. Create it once, then use the returned handle for multiple load/show cycles with the same ad-unit ID and creation configuration. ad_unit_id — Interstitial ad-unit ID from the LevelPlay dashboard. bid_floor — Optional minimum eCPM in USD. It applies to every load by this object; changing it requires destroying the handle and creating a new object. handle — Positive handle, or nil when native creation is rejected.

6741.content: levelplay.create_rewarded_ad(ad_unit_id: string, bid_floor?: number): number Creates a reusable rewarded ad object after successful initialization. Its ad-unit ID and optional bid floor are fixed for the object's lifetime. Create it once, then use the returned handle for multiple load/show cycles with the same ad-unit ID and creation configuration. ad_unit_id — Rewarded ad-unit ID from the LevelPlay dashboard. bid_floor — Optional minimum eCPM in USD. It applies to every load by this object; changing it requires destroying the handle and creating a new object. handle — Positive handle, or nil when native creation is rejected.

6742.content: levelplay.destroy_banner_ad(handle: number) Removes and destroys the banner view and invalidates its handle.

6743.content: levelplay.destroy_interstitial_ad(handle: number) Permanently releases an interstitial ad object, invalidates its handle, and stops callbacks for it. Do not destroy between ordinary impressions or during load/display when terminal callbacks are still required.

6744.content: levelplay.destroy_rewarded_ad(handle: number) Permanently releases a rewarded ad object, invalidates its handle, and stops callbacks for it. Do not destroy between ordinary impressions, and never destroy a displayed rewarded ad before its reward and close callbacks are received.

7331.content: realtime.MATCHMAKINGMODE_SERIAL_MATCHING Distributes players across available rooms sequentially but takes filters into account. Without filters, rooms get players evenly distributed.

7364.content: playables.load_data(callback: function) Loads serialized game data from YouTube. Only one load request may be in progress at a time. The request remains in progress until its callback returns, so the callback cannot start another load_data() request.

7365.content: playables.log_error() Reports an error occurrence to YouTube. Takes no arguments and returns no value. Reporting is best-effort and rate-limited, so delivery is not guaranteed.

7366.content: playables.log_warning() Reports a warning occurrence to YouTube. Takes no arguments and returns no value. Reporting is best-effort and rate-limited, so delivery is not guaranteed.

7367.content: playables.on_audio_enabled_change(callback: function | nil) Registers a callback for YouTube audio-setting changes. Before the callback runs, the extension automatically mutes the master sound group when audio is disabled, or unmutes it when audio is enabled and the game is not paused. A new callback replaces the previous one. Pass nil to unregister it. This function cannot be called from its own callback. callback — The event callback, or nil to unregister the current callback.

7368.content: playables.on_pause(callback: function | nil) Registers a callback for YouTube pause events. The extension automatically mutes the master sound group before the callback runs. A new callback replaces the previous one. Pass nil to unregister it. This function cannot be called from its own callback. A paused game is not guaranteed to resume. callback — The event callback, or nil to unregister the current callback.

7369.content: playables.on_resume(callback: function | nil) Registers a callback for YouTube resume events. Before the callback runs, the extension automatically unmutes the master sound group if YouTube audio is enabled, or keeps it muted if audio is disabled. A new callback replaces the previous one. Pass nil to unregister it. This function cannot be called from its own callback. callback — The event callback, or nil to unregister the current callback.

7370.content: playables.open_yt_content(content_id: string, content_type: number | undefined, callback: function) Requests that YouTube open a video or another Playable. The content type is optional and defaults to CONTENT_TYPE_VIDEO. Only one request may be in progress at a time. The request remains in progress until its callback returns, so the callback cannot start another open_yt_content() request. content_id — The YouTube video or Playable ID. content_type — CONTENT_TYPE_VIDEO or CONTENT_TYPE_PLAYABLE.

7371.content: playables.request_interstitial_ad(callback: function) Requests an interstitial ad. Success does not guarantee that an ad was shown. Do not use this API to grant rewards. Only one interstitial request may be in progress at a time. The request remains in progress until its callback returns, so the callback cannot start another request_interstitial_ad() request. Keep handling YouTube audio, pause, and resume events during ads.

7372.content: playables.request_rewarded_ad(reward_id: string, callback: function) Requests a rewarded ad. Grant a reward only when reward_earned is true. Only one rewarded request may be in progress at a time. The request remains in progress until its callback returns, so the callback cannot start another request_rewarded_ad() request. Keep handling YouTube audio, pause, and resume events during ads. reward_id — A stable ID unique to the reward type. Reuse it for each offer of that reward and do not include user data.

7373.content: playables.save_data(data: string, callback: function) Saves valid UTF-8 text to YouTube, with a maximum size of 3 MiB. Invalid UTF-8 returns false and an error through the callback before the SDK is called. Base64-encode binary data such as sys.serialize() output before saving. Only one save request may be in progress at a time. The request remains in progress until its callback returns, so the callback cannot start another save_data() request. data — The serialized game data as valid UTF-8 text. Embedded zero bytes are supported.

7374.content: playables.send_score(score: number, callback: function) Sends an integer score to YouTube. Use one consistent score dimension across the game. Only one request may be in progress at a time. The request remains in progress until its callback returns, so the callback cannot start another send_score() request. score — An integer no greater than JavaScript's maximum safe integer.

7534.content: push.cancel(id: number) Use this function to cancel a previously scheduled local push notification. The notification is identified by a numeric id as returned by push.schedule(). id — The numeric id of the local push notification

7535.content: push.get_all_scheduled(): table Returns a table with all data associated with all scheduled local push notifications. The table contains key, value pairs where the key is the push notification id and the value is a table with the notification data, corresponding to the data given by push.get_scheduled(id). Table with all data associated with all scheduled notifications.

7536.content: push.get_scheduled(id: number): table Returns a table with all data associated with a specified local push notification. The notification is identified by a numeric id as returned by push.schedule(). id — The numeric id of the local push notification. Table with all data associated with the notification.

7542.content: push.PRIORITY_DEFAULT The default notification priority. Only available on Android. [icon:android]

7543.content: push.PRIORITY_HIGH Priority for more important notifications or alerts. Only available on Android. [icon:android]

7544.content: push.PRIORITY_LOW Priority for items that are less important. Only available on Android. [icon:android]

7545.content: push.PRIORITY_MAX Set this priority for your application's most important items that require the user's prompt attention or input. Only available on Android. [icon:android]

7546.content: push.PRIORITY_MIN This priority is for items might not be shown to the user except under special circumstances, such as detailed notification logs. Only available on Android. [icon:android]

7547.content: push.register(notifications: table, callback: function) Send a request for push notifications. Note that the notifications table parameter is iOS only and will be ignored on Android. Register for push notifications on iOS. Note that the token needs to be converted on this platform. Register for push notifications on Android. notifications — The types of notifications to listen to. [icon:ios] callback — Register callback function.

7548.content: push.schedule(time: number, title: string, alert: string, payload: string, notification_settings: table): LuaMultiReturn<[number, string]> Local push notifications are scheduled with this function. The returned id value is uniquely identifying the scheduled notification and can be stored for later reference. This example demonstrates how to schedule a local notification: time — Number of seconds into the future until the notification should be triggered. title — Localized title to be displayed to the user if the application is not running. alert — Localized body message of the notification to be displayed to the user if the application is not running. payload — JSON string to be passed to the registered listener function. notification_settings — Table with notification and platform specific fields Unique id that can be used to cancel or inspect the notification Error string if something went wrong, otherwise nil

7549.content: push.set_badge_count(count: number) Set the badge count for application icon. This function is only available on iOS. [icon:ios] count — Badge count

7550.content: push.set_listener(listener: function) Sets a listener function to listen to push notifications. Set the push notification listener. listener — Listener callback function.

8226.content: steam.user_stats_download_leaderboard_entries(leaderboard: string, request: ELeaderboardDataRequest, start: number, end: number) Asks the Steam back-end for a set of rows in the leaderboard. This call is asynchronous, with the result returned in a listener callback with event set to LeaderboardScoresDownloaded_t. LeaderboardScoresDownloaded_t will contain a handle to pull the results from GetDownloadedLeaderboardEntries(). You can ask for more entries than exist, and it will return as many as do exist. k_ELeaderboardDataRequestGlobal requests rows in the leaderboard from the full table, with nRangeStart & nRangeEnd in the range [1, TotalEntries] k_ELeaderboardDataRequestGlobalAroundUser requests rows around the current user, nRangeStart being negate e.g. DownloadLeaderboardEntries( hLeaderboard, k_ELeaderboardDataRequestGlobalAroundUser, -3, 3 ) will return 7 rows, 3 before the user, 3 after k_ELeaderboardDataRequestFriends requests all the rows for friends of the current user https://partner.steamgames.com/doc/api/ISteamUserStats#DownloadLeaderboardEntries

8272.content: mpeg.rewind(handle: number) Rewind video to the beginning. handle — The video handle to rewind.

8273.content: mpeg.seek(handle: number, time: number, seek_exact: boolean) Seek to the specified time. Will seek to the last intra frame just before the desired time. handle — The video handle to seek on. time — Time to seek to. seek_exact — If value is true the function will seek to the exact time, otherwise it will seek to the last intra frame just before the desired time. Exact seeking can be slow, because all frames up to the seeked one have to be decoded on top of the previous intra frame. Defaults to false.
