8551.content: dev-masih / defarmy defarmy Groups game objects (soldiers) into armies, places them in a built-in or customized pattern, and moves and rotates each army as a group. Create an army with army_create and a soldier for each game object with soldier_create, then call soldier_move from each soldier's update and apply the position and rotation it returns.

8552.content: army_create(army_center_position: Vector3, army_initial_rotation: Quaternion, member_padding: number, is_sticky: boolean, army_pattern: Hash, pattern_func?: PatternFunc): number Creates a group of game objects (an army) with the given member padding and pattern, and returns its id. PATTERN.CUSTOMIZED requires pattern_func, which upstream asserts, and every other pattern ignores it. Any value outside PATTERN fails an assert. army_center_position — The army's center position. army_initial_rotation — The army's initial rotation. member_padding — The distance between members. is_sticky — Whether members are glued to their places in the army, rather than following them. It shows most while the army rotates. army_pattern — One of PATTERN. pattern_func — Builds the rows for PATTERN.CUSTOMIZED.

8553.content: army_debug_draw(army_id: number, debug_color: Vector4) Draws an army's center and facing for one frame, by posting draw_line to @render:. Call it every frame to keep it shown. army_id — The army's id. debug_color — The color of the lines.

8554.content: army_members(army_id: number): number[] Returns the ids of the soldiers in an army. The list is the army's own, so editing it edits the army. army_id — The army's id.

8555.content: army_remove(army_id: number) Removes an army and releases its members, which stay as soldiers in no army. army_id — The army's id.

8556.content: army_update_pattern(army_id: number, army_pattern: Hash, pattern_func?: PatternFunc) Changes an army's pattern and rearranges its members at once. PATTERN.CUSTOMIZED requires pattern_func, which upstream asserts, and every other pattern ignores it. army_id — The army's id. army_pattern — One of PATTERN. pattern_func — Builds the rows for PATTERN.CUSTOMIZED.

8557.content: army_update_position(army_id: number, army_center_position: Vector3) Moves an army's center. army_id — The army's id. army_center_position — The new center position.

8558.content: army_update_rotation(army_id: number, army_rotation: Quaternion) Rotates an army. army_id — The army's id. army_rotation — The new rotation.

8559.content: army_update_stickiness(army_id: number, is_sticky: boolean) Changes whether an army's members are glued to their places in it. army_id — The army's id. is_sticky — Whether members are glued to their places, rather than following them.

8560.content: PATTERN: { BOTTOM_TO_TOP_SQUARE: Hash; TOP_TO_BOTTOM_SQUARE: Hash; TRIANGLE: Hash; RHOMBUS_TALL: Hash; RHOMBUS_SHORT: Hash; CUSTOMIZED: Hash; } The army patterns army_create and army_update_pattern take. The five named patterns place the soldiers in built-in shapes. CUSTOMIZED takes its rows from the pattern_func passed beside it.

8561.content: soldier_create(position: Vector3, initial_direction: Vector3, army_id?: number): number Creates a soldier and returns its id, joining it to an army when army_id is given. position — The soldier's current position. initial_direction — The direction the soldier's game object faces at zero rotation. Every rotation soldier_move returns is relative to it. army_id — The army to join.

8562.content: soldier_debug_off(soldier_id: number) Turns off a soldier's debug marks. soldier_id — The soldier's id.

8563.content: soldier_debug_on(soldier_id: number, debug_color: Vector4) Turns on a soldier's debug marks: each soldier_move call then posts draw_line to @render: to mark the position the soldier is heading for with a cross. soldier_id — The soldier's id. debug_color — The color of the marks.

8564.content: soldier_join_army(soldier_id: number, army_id: number) Moves a soldier into an army, out of the army it was in. soldier_id — The soldier's id. army_id — The army's id.

8565.content: soldier_leave_army(soldier_id: number) Takes a soldier out of its army and rearranges the members left. A soldier in no army is left as it is. At v1 the rearrangement raises a Lua error when the soldier was the army's last member, so call army_remove instead in that case. soldier_id — The soldier's id.

8566.content: soldier_move(soldier_id: number, current_position: Vector3, speed: number, threshold?: number): LuaMultiReturn<[ Vector3, Quaternion ] | [ undefined, undefined ]> Calculates a soldier's next position and rotation, moving it toward its place in its army. A soldier in no army keeps current_position. Returns undefined for both values once the soldier is removed: const [position, rotation] = defarmy.soldier_move(id, go.get_position(), speed). soldier_id — The soldier's id. current_position — The soldier's current position. speed — How far the soldier moves this call. threshold — The distance from its place within which the soldier counts as placed. Defaults to 1.

8567.content: soldier_remove(soldier_id: number) Removes a soldier completely, rearranging the army it was in. soldier_move then returns undefined for both values. At v1 the rearrangement raises a Lua error when the soldier was the army's last member, so call army_remove first in that case. soldier_id — The soldier's id.

8591.content: dev-masih / defgraph defgraph Builds a world map as a graph of nodes and routes that can change at any time, draws it for debugging, and moves game objects along it with a built-in pathfinder. Add nodes with map_add_node and join them with map_add_route, start each game object with move_initialize, then call move_player from its update and apply the position and rotation it returns. MoveData MoveResult

8592.content: debug_draw_map_nodes(is_show_ids?: boolean) Draws every node for one frame, by posting draw_line and, for the ids, draw_text to @render:. A node with no route is drawn as a triangle, a dead end as a cross and an intersection as a square. Call it every frame to keep it shown. is_show_ids — Whether to draw each node's id beside it. Defaults to false.

8593.content: debug_draw_map_routes() Draws every route for one frame, by posting draw_line to @render:: two-way routes in one color, and one-way routes in another with a square near the end they run to. Call it every frame to keep it shown.

8594.content: debug_draw_player_move(movement_data: MoveData, color: Vector4, is_show_intersection?: boolean) Draws the rest of a game object's path for one frame, by posting draw_line to @render:. Nothing is drawn while the game object stands still for want of a route. Call it every frame to keep it shown. movement_data — The movement data from move_initialize or move_player. color — The color of the path. is_show_intersection — Whether to mark each point on the path with a cross. Defaults to false.

8595.content: debug_set_properties(node_color?: Vector4, two_way_route_color?: Vector4, one_way_route_color?: Vector4, draw_scale?: number) Sets the colors and the scale the debug_draw functions draw with. A nil keeps a value's current setting, and each starts at the default stated on it. node_color — The color of the nodes. Defaults to vmath.vector4(1, 0, 1, 1). two_way_route_color — The color of two-way routes. Defaults to vmath.vector4(0, 1, 0, 1). one_way_route_color — The color of one-way routes. Defaults to vmath.vector4(0, 1, 1, 1). draw_scale — The size of the node marks. Defaults to 5.

8596.content: map_add_node(position: Vector3): number Adds a node at a position and returns its id. The position's z is ignored. A node with no route takes no part in routing, so remove one that is no longer used. position — The node's position.

8597.content: map_add_route(source_id: number, destination_id: number, is_one_way?: boolean) Adds a route between two nodes, both ways unless is_one_way is true. A route from a node to itself is ignored, and an unknown id fails an assert. A one-way route is a little cheaper to path through when the other way is never needed. source_id — The node the route starts at. destination_id — The node the route ends at. is_one_way — Whether the route runs from source_id to destination_id only. Defaults to false.

8598.content: map_remove_node(node_id: number) Removes a node and every route attached to it. An unknown id fails an assert. node_id — The node's id.

8599.content: map_remove_route(source_id: number, destination_id: number, is_remove_one_way?: boolean) Removes the route between two nodes, both ways unless is_remove_one_way is true. An unknown id fails an assert. source_id — The node the route starts at. destination_id — The node the route ends at. is_remove_one_way — Whether to remove only the way from source_id to destination_id. Defaults to false.

8600.content: map_set_properties(settings_gameobject_threshold?: number, settings_path_curve_tightness?: number, settings_path_curve_roundness?: number, settings_path_curve_max_distance_from_corner?: number, settings_allow_enter_on_route?: boolean) Sets the module's path and movement settings, which every move_initialize call falls back to for a setting it is not given. A nil keeps a setting's current value, and each starts at the default stated on it. settings_gameobject_threshold — The distance within which a game object counts as on a route or at a point. Use a larger value for faster game objects; the smallest useful value is 1. Defaults to 1. settings_path_curve_tightness — How tight a turn on the path is; the smallest useful value is 2. Defaults to 4. settings_path_curve_roundness — How round a turn on the path is. 0 gives no curves and ignores the tightness and the corner distance, and a higher value costs more processing, most of all while nodes move. Defaults to 3. settings_path_curve_max_distance_from_corner — The farthest from its corner a turn may start. Defaults to 10. settings_allow_enter_on_route — Whether a game object may enter the map partway along a route, rather than only at a node. Defaults to true.

8601.content: map_update_node_position(node_id: number, position: Vector3) Moves an existing node, and the routes attached to it with it. An unknown id fails an assert. node_id — The node's id. position — The node's new position.

8602.content: move_initialize(source_position: Vector3, destination_list: number[], route_type?: Hash, initial_face_vector?: Vector3, settings_gameobject_threshold?: number, settings_path_curve_tightness?: number, settings_path_curve_roundness?: number, settings_path_curve_max_distance_from_corner?: number, settings_allow_enter_on_route?: boolean): MoveData Starts a game object moving from its position through a list of destination nodes, and returns the movement data move_player takes. Each setting it is not given falls back to the value map_set_properties set. To change the destinations, call it again and replace the old movement data with the result. source_position — The game object's current position. destination_list — The destination node ids, in order. With an empty list the game object stands still and move_player reports no destination_id. route_type — One of ROUTETYPE. Defaults to ROUTETYPE.ONETIME. initial_face_vector — The direction the game object faces at zero rotation. Without it, move_player returns no rotation. settings_gameobject_threshold — The distance within which the game object counts as on a route or at a point. Defaults to the map_set_properties value. settings_path_curve_tightness — How tight a turn on the path is. Defaults to the map_set_properties value. settings_path_curve_roundness — How round a turn on the path is, 0 for no curves. Defaults to the map_set_properties value. settings_path_curve_max_distance_from_corner — The farthest from its corner a turn may start. Defaults to the map_set_properties value. settings_allow_enter_on_route — Whether the game object may enter the map partway along a route. Defaults to the map_set_properties value.

8603.content: move_player(current_position: Vector3, speed: number, move_data: MoveData): LuaMultiReturn<[ MoveData, MoveResult ]> Moves a game object one step along its path toward its current destination, and returns the movement data and the result of the move: const [data, result] = defgraph.move_player(go.get_position(), speed dt, move). Keep the returned movement data in place of the one passed in. When the map has changed since the last call, the path is found again first. result.rotation is undefined unless move_initialize was given an initial_face_vector. current_position — The game object's current position. speed — How far the game object moves this call, its speed already multiplied by dt. move_data — The movement data from move_initialize or the last move_player.

8604.content: destination_index: number The 1-based index of the current destination in destination_list. ⚠️ 1-based; passed to defgraph unchanged.

8605.content: destination_list: number[] The destination node ids, the same list move_initialize was given.

8606.content: path_index: number The 1-based index of the next point on the path, or 0 while the game object stands still because the map has no route or destination_list is empty. ⚠️ 1-based; passed to defgraph unchanged.

8607.content: route_type: Hash The ROUTETYPE the game object moves by.

8608.content: destination_id: number The node id of the current destination.

8609.content: is_reached: boolean Whether the game object is at its destination. With more than one destination it reads true on reaching each one, then false again while destination_id moves on to the next.

8610.content: position: Vector3 The game object's next position.

8611.content: rotation: Quaternion | undefined The game object's next rotation around z, relative to the initial_face_vector passed to move_initialize. undefined when move_initialize was given none.

8612.content: ROUTETYPE: { ONETIME: Hash; SHUFFLE: Hash; CYCLE: Hash; } How move_initialize takes a game object through more than one destination. ONETIME visits them in order and stops at the last, SHUFFLE visits them in random order without stopping, and CYCLE visits them in order and starts over after the last. With one destination they all behave the same.

8634.content: Dragosha / defold-light-and-shadows · constants light_and_shadows.constants The light options the render script forwards into shader uniform constants. Scripts such as light_setting.script and sun.script write them, and light.update and the render script read them every frame. Vector fields are mutated in place (constants.fog.x = 20); assigning a new value to a field goes through a cast, since a namespace import is read-only. LightEntry

8635.content: ambient: Vector4 The ambient color, added after every light source is blended. w is the maximum value of each final color component.

8636.content: cam_look_at_position: Vector3 The point the camera looks at, the center of the shadow projection. light.update copies it from light.cam_look_at.

8637.content: cam_position: Vector4 The camera world position, which the shader uses for specular light. light.update copies it from light.cam_position.

8638.content: cam_z: number The camera Z coordinate, the distance from the focus point. light.update copies it from light.cam_z.

8639.content: clear_color: Vector4 The color that clears the default render target, which is the background color. RGB in 0..1.

8640.content: far_z: number The camera far Z plane. The reference render script reads it from the camera while light_and_shadows.get_far_near_z_from_camera is true.

8641.content: focus_range: number How wide the depth-of-field focus zone is. light_and_shadows.dof sets it from focus_range.

8642.content: fog_color: Vector4 The fog color, usually the clear color. w is the fog density from 0 to 1, where 0 is the densest.

8643.content: fog: Vector4 The minimum and maximum Z in camera view space between which the fog starts and ends, in x and y.

8644.content: color: Vector4 The color. w is the power after distance attenuation.

8645.content: direction?: Vector4 The spotlight direction; w above 0 turns the spotlight on. light_and_shadows.update sends a zero vector when it is absent.

8646.content: distance: number The squared distance from the point the camera looks at.

8647.content: position: Vector4 The world position. w carries the spotlight smoothness.

8648.content: power: number The power before distance attenuation.

8649.content: lights: LightEntry[] The light sources, their world positions and colors. Only the first light_and_shadows.max_lights reach the shader; missing ones are sent as zero vectors.

8650.content: near_z: number The camera near Z plane. The reference render script reads it from the camera while light_and_shadows.get_far_near_z_from_camera is true.

8651.content: shadow_color: Vector4 The inverted shadow color, subtracted where shadows fall. light_and_shadows.update sets w to 1 when light_and_shadows.shadow is on and 0 when it is off.

8653.content: sun_dir: Vector3 The sun direction, used for shadow casting with a perspective projection.

8654.content: sun_position: Vector4 The sun position, the one light source that casts shadows.

8678.content: Dragosha / defold-light-and-shadows · light light_and_shadows.light The light sources manager. It keeps the list of point light sources and the camera position, and each frame writes the sorted sources and the camera values into light_and_shadows.constants. light_setting.script calls set_color and update, and a scene controller calls set_position as its camera moves. Assigning a new value to a field goes through a cast, since a namespace import is read-only. LightSource

8679.content: attenuation_coefficient: number Divides a source's squared distance from the camera focus point before it scales the source's power.

8680.content: cam_look_at: Vector3 The point the camera looks at, set by set_position. Light sources are sorted by their distance from it.

8681.content: cam_position: Vector3 The camera world position, set by set_position.

8682.content: cam_view: Quaternion The camera rotation, set by set_position. A source with rotate set turns to it.

8683.content: cam_z: number The camera Z coordinate, the distance from the focus point that depth of field needs. Set it here or with set_position's cam_z.

8684.content: current_value?: Vector4 The color sent to the shader, its w attenuated by distance. update creates it from nothing when it is absent.

8685.content: direction: Vector4 The spotlight direction. w is the cone angle in radians; 0 or less turns the spotlight off.

8686.content: id?: Hash The game object id, as bulb.script stores it.

8687.content: num: number A positive number keeps the source out of the distance sort and always visible; the default is -1.

8688.content: position: Vector4 The world position. w carries the spotlight smoothness, from 0 (soft) to 1 (hard).

8689.content: rotate?: boolean When true, update rotates the game object to the camera rotation, as a billboard.

8690.content: static_spot?: boolean When true, update never reads the game object's rotation for the spotlight direction again.

8691.content: static?: boolean When true, update never reads the game object's world position again.

8692.content: timer?: number A timer bulb.script stores; update does not read it.

8693.content: value: Vector4 The color in x, y, z. w is the power update attenuates by distance; bulb.script sets it to 1 / power.

8694.content: y_offset?: number Added to the world Y position each frame.

8695.content: list: LuaTable<Hash, LightSource> Every point light source, keyed by its game object id. update reads it every frame.

8696.content: reset(self: object) Clears the light sources sent to the shader and restores the module's default ambient, fog color and fog constants. self — Unused.

8697.content: set_color(fog_color?: Vector4, fog?: Vector4, ambient?: Vector4, clear_color?: Vector4) Sets the base light uniform constants in light_and_shadows.constants. An omitted value leaves its constant as it is. It also posts clear_color to @render: with clear_color, or fog_color when that is omitted. fog_color — The fog color in RGB; w is the fog density. fog — The minimum and maximum Z in camera view space where the fog begins and ends. ambient — The ambient color. clear_color — The color that clears the default render target, which is the background color.

8698.content: set_position(cam_rotation: Quaternion, cam_look_at_position: Vector3, cam_position: Vector3, cam_z?: number) Sets the camera rotation, the point the camera looks at, and the camera position. cam_rotation — The camera rotation. cam_look_at_position — The point the camera looks at. cam_position — The camera world position. cam_z — The camera Z coordinate, the distance from the focus point, for depth of field. Omitted, cam_z keeps its value.

8699.content: top_v: Vector3 The up vector, rotated by a game object's world rotation to give a spotlight's direction.

8700.content: update(self: object, dt: number) Prepares the constants for the render script: updates each source's position and spotlight direction from its game object, sorts the sources by distance from the point the camera looks at into light_and_shadows.constants.lights, attenuates their power, and copies the camera values. Call it from update. self — Unused. dt — Unused.

8733.content: Dragosha / defold-light-and-shadows · light_and_shadows light_and_shadows.light_and_shadows Real-time shadows from one light source, the sun, and many point light sources, wired into a render script. Call init(self) from the render script's init, update(self) from its update, and draw_upscaled(self) after drawing the world when a post effect is on (see light_and_shadows/render/default.render_script, the lines marked -- L_S Injection). The settings fields are read every frame. Vector fields are mutated in place; assigning a new value to any other field goes through a cast, since a namespace import is read-only: (light_and_shadows as { fxaa: boolean }).fxaa = true. SizedRenderTarget DofOptions

8734.content: blur_power: number How strong the blur is, 1 to 10. The default is 2.5.

8735.content: blur_resolution: number How much the blur render target is reduced in size, for speed. The default is 2.

8736.content: blur: boolean Whether the game scene is blurred, so an unblurred GUI can be drawn on top. It uses the same render target as upscaling. The default is false.

8737.content: depth_bias: number The shadow depth bias. Too high a bias detaches shadows from their objects; too low a bias causes shadow acne. The default is 0.0004.

8738.content: discard_threshold: number The alpha below which the sprite shader discards semitransparent pixels. The default is 0.5.

8739.content: dof(enable: boolean, options?: DofOptions) Turns depth of field on or off. enable — true turns depth of field on. options — The depth-of-field options. Omitted, every setting keeps its value.

8740.content: blur_power?: number How strong the blur effect is, 2 to 10. Omitted, blur_power keeps its value.

8741.content: blur_resolution: number How much the blur render target is reduced in size, for speed; 1 to 2 is enough. dof copies it with no fallback, so it is required: an options table without it leaves blur_resolution nil and the next update fails.

8742.content: focus_range?: number How wide the focus zone is, 0.1 to 4. Omitted, focus_range in light_and_shadows.constants keeps its value.

8743.content: upscale?: boolean Whether to upscale the main render target. dof sets upscale to false when it is omitted.

8744.content: draw_upscaled(self: object) Blurs the main render target when depth of field or blur is on, then draws it to the screen, with FXAA when fxaa is on. Call it after the world is drawn to the main render target. The render script's self.predicates must carry upscale. self — The render script instance.

8745.content: focus: Vector4 The depth-of-field focus position, in z.

8746.content: fxaa: boolean Whether FXAA anti-aliasing is applied to the final image. The default is false.

8747.content: get_far_near_z_from_camera: boolean Whether the reference render script reads the near and far Z planes from the camera component into light_and_shadows.constants. Set it to false to set near_z and far_z by hand. The default is true.

8748.content: init(self: object) Sets up the shadow map, the orthographic shadow projection and the render constants on the render script. Call it from the render script's init. self — The render script instance.

8749.content: max_lights: number How many point light sources the shader processes at once, at most 16. The default is 8.

8750.content: mix: boolean Whether depth of field is on. dof sets it. The default is false.

8751.content: polygon_offset: { factor: number; units: number; } The polygon offset applied while drawing the shadow map. Raise it to reduce shadow acne; lower it if shadows detach from their casters.

8752.content: render_shadows(self: object) Draws every object tagged shadow into the shadow map. update calls it while shadow is on. The render script's self.predicates must carry shadow, shadow_local, shadow_instanced, shadow_instanced_billboard, shadow_instanced_textured, shadow_skinned_instanced and shadow_skinned. self — The render script instance.

8753.content: render_target(name: string, w: number, h: number, no_depth?: boolean): SizedRenderTarget Returns the render target named name, creating it with a color buffer and, unless no_depth is set, a depth texture. A target that exists at another size is resized. name — The render target name, also its key in rt_list. w — The width in pixels. h — The height in pixels. no_depth — true creates the target without a depth buffer.

8754.content: rt_list: LuaTable<string, SizedRenderTarget> Every render target render_target created, keyed by name.

8755.content: set_orthographic_projection(proj_w: number, proj_h: number, near_z?: number, far_z?: number) Sets an orthographic shadow projection, used for directional light. init sets one. proj_w — The width of the area the shadow is projected on. proj_h — The height of the area the shadow is projected on. near_z — The near clipping plane. The default is -500. far_z — The far clipping plane. The default is 500.

8756.content: set_perspective_projection(fov?: number, aspect?: number, near_z?: number, far_z?: number) Sets a perspective shadow projection, cast in the direction of sun_dir in light_and_shadows.constants. Experimental. fov — The field of view in radians. The default is 3.14 / 1.5. aspect — The aspect ratio. The default is 1. near_z — The near clipping plane. The default is 50. far_z — The far clipping plane. The default is 500.

8757.content: shadow: boolean Whether the sun casts shadows. The default is true.

8758.content: h: number The height in pixels.

8760.content: w: number The width in pixels.

8761.content: update_light(self: object) Writes the sun, the point light sources, the ambient and fog values and the camera values from light_and_shadows.constants into the render constants. update calls it. self — The render script instance.

8762.content: update(self: object) Updates the light constants, draws the shadow map, and creates or resizes the main and blur render targets a post effect needs. Call it from the render script's update. self — The render script instance.

8763.content: upscale: boolean Whether the main render target is upscaled. When on, every object is first rendered to a render target no larger than the project settings size, which is then placed on the screen with linear scaling. Add light_and_shadows/props/render_target_quad.go to the main scene to use it. The default is false.

8764.content: zoom: number The zoom update computed for upscaling, 1 when upscale is off.

8785.content: Dragosha / defold-sprite-repeat · node_repeat node_repeat GUI box node texture repeat (tiling) shader helper: reads a box node's atlas animation and drives the repeat material's constants. NodeRepeatAnimation RepeatFrame

8786.content: create(node_or_string: Opaque<"node"> | string, animation_id: Hash | string | undefined, atlas_path: Hash | string): NodeRepeatAnimation Reads an atlas animation's frames for a GUI box node that uses the repeat material, and returns a handle that applies them. Call it from a GUI script. Apply the repeat material to the node first, and disable sprite trim mode for the atlas images: every frame must have exactly 8 UV values, or this asserts. Walks the atlas animation's frame list, so it needs Defold 1.12.3 or later. node_or_string — The box node, or its id. animation_id — The atlas animation to read. Pass undefined to use the node's current flipbook. atlas_path — The atlas resource path, passed to resource.get_atlas. Asserted present.

8787.content: get_screen_aspect_ratio(): LuaMultiReturn<[ number, number ]> Measures how the window is stretched relative to the GUI's design size, stores the result in x_ratio and y_ratio, and returns it. The smaller ratio is always 1. Call it from a GUI script. The horizontal and vertical ratios.

8788.content: animate(repeat_x: number, repeat_y: number) Applies the first frame and the repeat factors to the node. When the animation has more than one frame and a non-zero fps, starts a repeating timer that steps through the frames. repeat_x — How many times the image repeats horizontally. repeat_y — How many times the image repeats vertically.

8789.content: current_frame: number The 1-based index of the frame shown next. ⚠️ 1-based; passed to node_repeat unchanged.

8790.content: fps: number The animation's playback rate, from the atlas.

8791.content: frames: RepeatFrame[] Every frame of the animation, in playback order.

8792.content: handle?: number The timer.delay handle driving playback. Present only while a multi-frame animation plays.

8793.content: height: number The animation's height, from the atlas.

8794.content: node: Opaque<"node"> The box node the animation drives.

8795.content: stop() Cancels the playback timer, if one is running.

8796.content: update(repeat_x?: number, repeat_y?: number) Changes the repeat factors and applies them to the node. A factor left out keeps its current value. repeat_x — How many times the image repeats horizontally. repeat_y — How many times the image repeats vertically.

8797.content: v: Vector4 The uv_repeat value: x/y the repeat factors, z/w the current frame's size.

8798.content: width: number The animation's width, from the atlas.

8799.content: h: number The frame's height in texture pixels.

8800.content: uv_coord: Vector4 The frame's UV rectangle in the texture: x/y one corner, z/w the other.

8801.content: uv_rotated: Vector4 (0, 1, 0, 0) when the atlas stores the frame rotated clockwise, else (1, 0, 0, 0).

8802.content: w: number The frame's width in texture pixels.

8803.content: x_ratio: number The horizontal stretch of the window relative to the GUI's design size, divided by the smaller of the two stretches. Starts at 1; get_screen_aspect_ratio updates it.

8804.content: y_ratio: number The vertical stretch of the window relative to the GUI's design size, divided by the smaller of the two stretches. Starts at 1; get_screen_aspect_ratio updates it.

8820.content: Dragosha / defold-sprite-repeat · sprite_repeat sprite_repeat Sprite texture repeat (tiling) shader helper: reads a sprite's atlas animation and drives the repeat material's constants. SpriteRepeatAnimation RepeatFrame

8821.content: create(sprite_url: Url | Hash | string, sprite_id?: Hash | string, self?: { atlas_data?: ReturnType<typeof resource.get_atlas>; tex_info?: ReturnType<typeof resource.get_texture_info>; }): SpriteRepeatAnimation Reads an atlas animation's frames for a sprite that uses the repeat material, and returns a handle that applies them. Apply the repeat material to the sprite first, and disable sprite trim mode for the atlas images: every frame must have exactly 8 UV values, or this asserts. Walks the atlas animation's frame list, so it needs Defold 1.12.3 or later. sprite_url — The sprite component. sprite_id — The atlas animation to read. When omitted, the sprite's current animation is used. self — The calling script's self. When it already holds atlas_data and tex_info, they are reused instead of read again; otherwise they are read and stored on it, so later calls for sprites sharing the atlas skip the lookup.

8822.content: h: number The frame's height in texture pixels.

8823.content: uv_coord: Vector4 The frame's UV rectangle in the texture: x/y one corner, z/w the other.

8824.content: uv_rotated: Vector4 (0, 1, 0, 0) when the atlas stores the frame rotated clockwise, else (1, 0, 0, 0).

8825.content: w: number The frame's width in texture pixels.

8847.content: elefant-ai / player2-ai-npc-defold ainpc AI NPCs for Defold through the Player2 desktop app: chat completions, spawned NPCs to talk to, and a stream of their responses.

8848.content: chat_completion(body: Body | string, on_reply: ReplyCallback, on_fail: FailCallback) Requests a chat completion. A string is sent as one user message: the extension pastes it into {"messages":[{"content":"<text>","role":"user"}]} without escaping, so text holding a quote, a backslash or a newline makes invalid JSON. Pass a body with a messages list to send arbitrary text. body — The request body, or the text of one user message. on_reply — Called with the completion. on_fail — Called when the request fails.

8850.content: npc_kill(npc_id: string, on_reply: ReplyCallback, on_fail: FailCallback) Removes a spawned NPC. npc_id — The NPC to remove. on_reply — Called when the NPC is removed. on_fail — Called when the request fails. npc_kill(game_id: string, npc_id: string, on_reply: ReplyCallback, on_fail: FailCallback) Removes a spawned NPC. game_id — Accepted but not sent: the request path keeps the literal {game_id} placeholder. npc_id — The NPC to remove. on_reply — Called when the NPC is removed. on_fail — Called when the request fails.

8851.content: npc_responses(on_receive: ReplyCallback, on_finish: (self: unknown) => void, on_fail: FailCallback): number Opens the stream of NPC responses. Without a game_id the request path keeps the literal {game_id} placeholder. on_receive — Called with each chunk the stream delivers, decoded as JSON when it parses, otherwise as text. on_finish — Called when the stream ends, after on_fail when it failed. on_fail — Called when the stream fails. The stream id, for {@link ainpc.stop_npc_responses}. npc_responses(game_id: string, on_receive: ReplyCallback, on_finish: (self: unknown) => void, on_fail: FailCallback): number Opens the stream of NPC responses for a game. game_id — The game whose responses to stream; it replaces {game_id} in the request path. on_receive — Called with each chunk the stream delivers, decoded as JSON when it parses, otherwise as text. on_finish — Called when the stream ends, after on_fail when it failed. on_fail — Called when the stream fails. The stream id, for {@link ainpc.stop_npc_responses}.

8852.content: npc_spawn(body: Body, on_reply: ReplyCallback, on_fail: FailCallback) Spawns an NPC. body — The NPC definition, such as the name, short_name, character_description, system_prompt and voice_id the upstream example sends. on_reply — Called with the spawn reply. on_fail — Called when the request fails. npc_spawn(game_id: string, body: Body | string, on_reply: ReplyCallback, on_fail: FailCallback) Spawns an NPC from a body given as a table or as JSON text. game_id — Accepted but not sent: the request path keeps the literal {game_id} placeholder. This form is the only one that takes the body as JSON text. body — The NPC definition, or JSON text sent as it is. on_reply — Called with the spawn reply. on_fail — Called when the request fails.

8853.content: stop_npc_responses(stream_id: number) Stops a stream opened by {@link ainpc.npc_responses}. An id that names no open stream is ignored. stream_id — The id npc_responses returned.

9029.content: defwin.fit_shrink(ratio?: number) Fit the window to the given aspect ratio by only shrinking the size in one direction. ratio — The aspect ratio to fit to (width / height). If omitted, the aspect ratio from the display size in game.project is used.

9035.content: defwin.lock_ratio(ratio?: number) Lock the aspect ratio of the window when the user drags its border. ratio — The aspect ratio to lock (width / height). If omitted, the aspect ratio of the default resolution in game.project is used.

9039.content: defwin.request_quit() Request to quit the game, behaving as if the user pressed the close button or Alt+F4. Triggers the close listener and delay handling.

The transparent areas will also be click-through. r — Red component in [0.0, 1.0]. If omitted, the render clear color is used. g — Green component in [0.0, 1.0]. b — Blue component in [0.0, 1.0].

9043.content: defwin.set_border_color_none() Set the window border color to be transparent.

9045.content: defwin.set_borderless(enable: boolean) Remove or restore the window border. enable — true to remove the window border, false to restore it

9046.content: defwin.set_caption_color(r?: number, g?: number, b?: number) Set window caption color. r — Red component in [0.0, 1.0]. If omitted, the default color is used. g — Green component in [0.0, 1.0]. b — Blue component in [0.0, 1.0].

9047.content: defwin.set_caption_text_color(r?: number, g?: number, b?: number) Set window caption text color. r — Red component in [0.0, 1.0]. If omitted, the default color is used. g — Green component in [0.0, 1.0]. b — Blue component in [0.0, 1.0].

9057.content: defwin.set_minimum_window_size(width: number, height?: number) Set the minimum size a window is allowed to have when resized. width — Minimum width in pixels. height — Minimum height in pixels.

9058.content: defwin.set_progress_error() Set the progress bar on the taskbar button to an error state, turning it red.

9059.content: defwin.set_progress_load() Set the progress bar on the taskbar button to an indeterminate loading state.

9060.content: defwin.set_progress(value: number) Set the progress bar on the taskbar button. value — Progress in [0.0, 1.0]

9061.content: defwin.set_rtl_layout(enable: boolean) Set window bar layout to right-to-left, affecting buttons, title, and icon. enable — Set window to RTL layout on true, and to LTR layout on false

9062.content: defwin.set_tool_window(enable: boolean) Turns the window into a tool window. Tool windows are not shown on taskbar and Alt-Tab, and have no minimize and maximize buttons or icon. enable — Set to tool window on true, and back to normal window on false

9063.content: defwin.start_drag() Start dragging the window along the cursor. Must be paired with repeated calls to update_drag() to have any effect.

9064.content: defwin.start_flash(taskbar: boolean, caption: boolean, until_focused: boolean, timeout?: number) Start flashing the window until manually stopped or until the window regains focus. taskbar — Should the taskbar button flash caption — Should the window caption flash until_focused — If true, focusing the window stops the flash. 9065.content: defwin.stop_drag() Stop dragging the window along the cursor.

9066.content: defwin.stop_flash() Stop the window from flashing. As the current flash cycle still completes, it can take a few seconds to disappear.

9067.content: defwin.unlock_ratio() Remove the aspect ratio lock set by lock_ratio.

9068.content: defwin.update_drag() Update one frame of the window drag started with start_drag(). Should be called every frame (e.g. from an on_input or update callback) while dragging is active.

9850.content: get_modules_download_progress(module_names: string | string[]): liveupdater_download_progress Byte-based progress for a module or a set of modules, with a per-resolution breakdown in the low/high fields. Shared dependency archives are counted once per set; an archive identical in both manifests counts toward the resolution counted first (for RES_BOTH that is lowres — the pass that actually downloads it). Anchored to the download queue: an archive counts as downloaded when nothing for it is pending, so the result reaches 100 exactly when the set's downloads drain. For by_request modules that were not requested yet, the future queue content is predicted from the same rules enqueue_modules uses; that prediction can dip for a moment while a shared archive is remounted to its highres copy, it recovers on the next mount.

9977.content: indiesoftby / defold-dissolve-fx dissolve_fx A dissolve effect for sprites. Add a noise and a ramp image to the sprite's atlas and set dissolve_fx/materials/sprite.material as the sprite's material, then call init from the script's init. The noise drives the dissolve and the ramp colors its burning edge.

9978.content: find_uvrect(sprite_url: string | Hash | Url, image_id: string, scale_mode?: ScaleMode): LuaMultiReturn<[ number, number, number, number ]> Finds an image in the sprite's atlas and returns its uv rect in texture space as four values: center x, center y, width and height: const [x, y, w, h] = dissolve_fx.find_uvrect("#sprite", "noise"). Upstream asserts that image_id is a string, that the atlas holds the image, and that the image is not trimmed (trim mode off, 8 uvs). With scale_mode, the width and height are also divided by the size of the sprite's current animation, so the vertex shader can map the noise from local positions. sprite_url — The sprite component. image_id — The image's id in the sprite's atlas. scale_mode — How the width and height are scaled to the sprite. Upstream asserts stretch or cover. When omitted, they are left in texture space.

9979.content: init(sprite_url: string | Hash | Url, noise_image: string, ramp_image: string, noise_scale_mode?: ScaleMode) Sets the sprite's noise_uvrect and ramp_uvrect from the two images in its atlas. The sprite must use the dissolve_fx/materials/sprite.material material. The effect is then driven by the sprite's dissolve.z property, the size of the burning edge, and dissolve.w, from 0 to 1, through go.set and go.animate: go.animate("#sprite", "dissolve.w", go.PLAYBACK_LOOP_PINGPONG, 1, go.EASING_LINEAR, 3). sprite_url — The sprite component with the dissolve material. noise_image — The noise image's id in the sprite's atlas. ramp_image — The ramp image's id in the sprite's atlas. noise_scale_mode — How the noise is scaled to the sprite. Defaults to stretch.

Defaults to false. result — The shuffled array (a new table, or the same table if inplace is true).

10224.content: splitmix64.weightedchoice(t: table): any Takes table t where keys are choices and values are weights. Returns a random key. If all weights are 0 or a weight is negative, an error is raised. t — Table of key-weight pairs. key — Random key chosen by weight.

10900.content: create(callback?: ((...args: any[]) => unknown) | event | undefined, callback_context?: unknown | undefined): event Generate a new event instance. This instance can then be used to subscribe to and trigger events. The callback function will be called when the event is triggered. The callback_context parameter is optional and will be passed as the first parameter to the callback function. Usually, it is used to pass the self instance. local e = event.create() local e = event.create(function(self) print("ok") end, self) callback — The function to be called when the event is triggered. Or the event instance to subscribe. callback_context — The first parameter to be passed to the callback function. A new event instance.

10906.content: clear() Remove all callbacks subscribed to the event, effectively resetting it. on_click_event:clear()

10907.content: is_empty(): boolean Check if the event has no subscribed callbacks. local is_empty = on_click_event:is_empty() True if the event has no subscribed callbacks

10908.content: is_subscribed(callback: ((...args: any[]) => unknown) | event, callback_context?: unknown | undefined): LuaMultiReturn<[boolean, number | undefined]> Determine if a specific callback is currently subscribed to the event. The callback_context should be the same as the one used when subscribing the callback. local is_subscribed = on_click_event:is_subscribed(callback, self) callback — The callback function in question. Or the event instance to check. callback_context — The first parameter to be passed to the callback function. True if the callback is subscribed to the event Index of callback in event if subscribed (return first found index)

10909.content: subscribe_once(callback: ((...args: any[]) => unknown) | event, callback_context?: unknown | undefined): boolean Subscribe a callback for a single trigger. After the first trigger the callback is automatically unsubscribed. on_click_event:subscribe_once(function(self) print("one-time click!") end, self) callback — The function or event to run once. callback_context — Same as subscribe. True if subscribed

10910.content: subscribe(callback: ((...args: any[]) => unknown) | event, callback_context?: unknown | undefined): boolean Subscribe a callback to the event or other event. The callback will be invoked whenever the event is triggered. The callback_context parameter is optional and will be passed as the first parameter to the callback function. If the callback with context is already subscribed, the warning will be logged. local function callback(self) print("clicked!") end on_click_event:subscribe(callback, self) -- Subscribe an event to another event event_1 = event.create(callback) event_2 = event.create() event_2:subscribe(event_1) -- Now event2 will trigger event1 callback — The function to be executed when the event occurs. callback_context — The first parameter to be passed to the callback function. True if event is subscribed (Will return false if the callback is already subscribed)

10911.content: trigger(...args: unknown[]): unknown Trigger the event, causing all subscribed callbacks to be executed. Any parameters passed to trigger will be forwarded to the callbacks. The return value of the last executed callback is returned. The event:trigger(...) can be called as event(...). on_click_event:trigger("arg1", "arg2") -- The event can be triggered as a function on_click_event("arg1", "arg2") ...args — Any number of parameters to be passed to the subscribed callbacks. Result of the last triggered callback

10912.content: unsubscribe(callback: ((...args: any[]) => unknown) | event, callback_context?: unknown | undefined): boolean Remove a previously subscribed callback from the event. The callback_context should be the same as the one used when subscribing the callback. If there is no callback_context provided, all callbacks with the same function will be unsubscribed. on_click_event:unsubscribe(callback, self) callback — The callback function to unsubscribe. callback_context — The first parameter to be passed to the callback function. If not provided, will unsubscribe all callbacks with the same function. True if event is unsubscribed

10916.content: reject_cancel_children() Reject pending child promises when a settled promise is cancelled.

10917.content: append(task: ((value: unknown) => unknown) | promise): promise Append a task to this promise's internal sequence without reassigning. The task may return a value or a promise. If task is a promise, the pipeline waits for it to finish and adopts its result. The incoming value is not forwarded into task (same as append(function() return task end)). Returns self for chaining. Almost similar to promise = promise:next(task), but without reassigning the promise. pipeline:append(step1) pipeline:append(step2) pipeline:append(step3) local last = pipeline:tail() print("Is going to check status of", last:is_pending())

10918.content: cancel() Cancel in-progress work in this promise chain. A pending promise is rejected with the cancelled reason and on_cancel runs. A settled promise is left as-is; pending descendants linked via next / append / adopt are still rejected, and they trigger the shared on_cancel. If nothing is still pending, this is a no-op. my_promise:cancel()

10919.content: catch(on_rejected: ((...args: any[]) => unknown) | event, context?: unknown | undefined): promise Attach a rejection handler to the promise. Equivalent to next(nil, on_rejected). load_data():catch(function(err) print("Failed:", err) end) on_rejected — Handler called when promise is rejected. context — The context to call the handler with. A new promise representing the result of the handler.

10920.content: finally(on_finally: ((...args: any[]) => unknown) | event, context?: unknown | undefined): promise Attach a handler that is called regardless of whether the promise is resolved or rejected. The handler is called with the resolved value or rejection reason. When context is provided, it is passed as the first argument. The handler return value is ignored. load_data():finally(function() hide_loading_spinner() end) on_finally — Handler called when promise is finished (resolved or rejected). context — The context to call the handler with. A new promise that resolves/rejects with the same value/reason as the original.

10922.content: is_finished(): boolean Check if the promise is finished (either resolved or rejected). True if the promise is finished.

10923.content: is_pending(): boolean Check if the promise is in pending state. True if the promise is pending.

10924.content: is_rejected(): boolean Check if the promise is in rejected state. True if the promise is rejected.

10925.content: is_resolved(): boolean Check if the promise is in resolved state. True if the promise is resolved.

10926.content: next(on_resolved?: ((...args: any[]) => unknown) | promise | event | undefined, on_rejected?: ((...args: any[]) => unknown) | promise | event | undefined, context?: unknown | undefined): promise Attach resolve and reject handlers to the promise. Returns a new promise that will be resolved or rejected based on the handlers' return values. load_data():next(function(data) return process(data) end):next(display):catch(show_error) on_resolved — Handler called when promise is resolved. If nil, value passes through. on_rejected — Handler called when promise is rejected. If nil, rejection passes through. context — The context to call the handlers with. A new promise representing the result of the handlers.

10933.content: value: unknown The resolved value or rejection reason

10936.content: clear() Remove all events and handlers from this queue instance, effectively resetting it. my_queue:clear()

10937.content: clear_events() Clear all pending events in this queue. my_queue:clear_events()

10939.content: get_events(): queue_event_data[] Get all pending events in this queue. for , event_data in ipairs(my_queue:get_events()) do print(event_data.data) end A table of pending events.

10940.content: has_subscribers(): boolean Check if this queue instance has no subscribed handlers. if my_queue:has_subscribers() then my_queue:push(data) end True if the queue instance has subscribed handlers

10941.content: is_empty(): boolean Check if this queue has no pending events. if my_queue:is_empty() then return end True if the queue has no pending events

10942.content: is_subscribed(handler: ((...args: any[]) => unknown) | event, context?: unknown | undefined): LuaMultiReturn<[boolean, number | undefined]> Check if a handler is subscribed to this queue instance. local ok = my_queue:is_subscribed(on_save, self) handler — The handler function or event to check. context — The context that was passed when subscribing. True if handler is subscribed Index of handler if subscribed

10943.content: process_next(event_handler?: ((...args: any[]) => unknown) | event | undefined, context?: unknown | undefined): boolean Process exactly one queued event with a specific handler (subscribers will NOT be called). If the handler returns non-nil the event will be removed from the queue. local handled = my_queue:process_next(function(data) return handle(data) end) event_handler — Specific handler or event to process the event. If this function returns non-nil, the event will be removed from the queue. context — The context to be passed to the handler. True if the head event was handled and removed

10944.content: process(event_handler: ((...args: any[]) => unknown) | event, context?: unknown | undefined) Process all events in this queue immediately. Subscribers will not be called in this function. Events can be handled and removed in event handler callback. If event is handled, it will be removed from the queue. my_queue:process(function(self, data) return handle(data) end, self) event_handler — Specific handler or event to process the events. If this function returns non-nil, the event will be removed from the queue. context — The context to be passed to the handler.

10945.content: push(data: unknown, on_handle?: ((...args: any[]) => unknown) | event | undefined, context?: unknown | undefined) Push a new event to the queue. The event will exist until it's handled by a subscriber. If there are already subscribers for this queue instance, they will be called immediately. If multiple subscribers handle the event, all subscribers will still be called. The on_handle callback will be called for each subscriber that handles the event. my_queue:push(save_data) my_queue:push(save_data, function() print("saved!") end) data — The data associated with the event. on_handle — Callback function or event to be called when the event is handled. context — The context to be passed as the first parameter to the on_handle function when the event is handled.

10946.content: subscribe_once(handler: ((...args: any[]) => unknown) | event, context?: unknown | undefined): boolean Subscribe a handler until it handles one event. The handler is invoked for each event in the queue until it returns non-nil (handles an event) then it is automatically unsubscribed and will not be invoked again, even if more events remain in the queue. my_queue:subscribe_once(function(self, data) return process(data) end, self) handler — The handler function or event to be called when an event is pushed. context — The context to be passed as the first parameter to the handler function. True if handler was subscribed successfully

10947.content: subscribe(handler: ((...args: any[]) => unknown) | event, context?: unknown | undefined): boolean Subscribe a handler to this queue instance. When an event is pushed to this queue, the handler will be called. If there are already events in the queue, they will be processed immediately. Return a non-nil value from the handler to mark the event as handled and remove it from the queue. local function on_save(self, data) do_save(data) return true end my_queue:subscribe(on_save, self) handler — The handler function or event to be called when an event is pushed. context — The context to be passed as the first parameter to the handler function. True if handler was subscribed successfully

10948.content: unsubscribe(handler: ((...args: any[]) => unknown) | event, context?: unknown | undefined): boolean Unsubscribe a handler from this queue instance. my_queue:unsubscribe(on_save, self) handler — The handler function or event to unsubscribe. context — The context that was passed when subscribing. True if handler was unsubscribed successfully

Migrations are used to update the game state in case of changes to the game state structure. Migrations are applied in order. Each migration should be a function that takes the game state as a parameter and returns the updated game state. local migrations = { -- Migration 1 function(game_state, logger) -- Assume we have new level_data field in the game state and we need to move level and score to it game_state.game.level_data = { level = game_state.game.level, score = game_state.game.score } game_state.game.level = nil game_state.game.score = nil return game_state }, -- Migration 2 function(game_state, logger) -- Just an example, multiply the score by 1000. For example we changed our score system game_state.game.level_data.score = game_state.game.level_data.score 1000 return game_state } } saver.set_migrations(migrations) saver.init() saver.bind_save_state("game", game_state) saver.apply_migrations() migrations_table — Array of migration functions

12980.content: set_blacklist(blacklist_components?: LuaTable | druid_component[] | undefined): druid_instance Set blacklist components for input processing. If blacklist is set, the listed components and their descendants are skipped on the input step. An empty list and nil both deny nobody. Descendants created later still match. The filter is scoped to the caller: on the druid instance it affects all components, on the self.druid inside a component it affects this component subtree only. Descendants created later still match, no need to call this again. The filter is scoped to the caller: on the druid instance it affects all components, on the self.druid inside a component it affects this component subtree only. 13569.content: iapm.buy(id: string) Start a purchase for a Myket one-time product. id — product to buy

13570.content: iapm.finish(transaction: table) Consume a product transaction. Call this only for consumable products and only after content delivery succeeds. Calling iapm.finish is required for a consumable transaction if auto_finish_transactions is disabled in project settings. Calling this function with auto_finish_transactions enabled is ignored and a warning is printed. The transaction.state field must equal iapm.TRANS_STATE_PURCHASED. Calling this for a transaction whose type is subs is ignored. transaction — transaction table parameter as supplied in listener callback

13571.content: iapm.list(ids: table, callback: function) Get details for the requested Myket one-time products and subscriptions. ids — table (array) of identifiers to get products from callback — result callback taking the following parameters

13574.content: iapm.restore(): boolean Restore owned, unconsumed products and active subscriptions. Results are sent to the listener registered with set_listener. Subscriptions are never consumed. success — value is true if current store supports handling restored transactions, otherwise false.

13575.content: iapm.set_listener(listener: function) Set the callback function to receive purchase transaction events. listener — listener callback function. Pass an empty function if you no longer wish to receive callbacks.

13576.content: iapm.set_public_key(public_key: string): boolean Set or replace the Base64-encoded Myket application public key used for local SHA1withRSA purchase-signature verification. Call this before set_listener, buy, or restore. Prefer the iap.public_key game.project setting so the key is available while pending purchases are processed. public_key — The application public key from the Myket developer panel. valid — true when the value is a valid Base64-encoded RSA public key; false otherwise.

13577.content: iapm.subscribe(id: string) Start a purchase for a Myket subscription. The result is delivered to the listener registered with set_listener. Subscriptions are never consumed, regardless of the auto_finish_transactions setting. An error is delivered when the installed Myket client does not support subscriptions. id — subscription product identifier

13655.content: voronoi.get_delauney_edges(diagram: userdata): table Returns the Delauney edges produced by the upstream jcv_delauney iterator. Each entry contains edge, sites, and pos fields matching jcv_delauney_edge. The upstream spelling "delauney" is preserved in the Lua function name. diagram — Generated diagram context. edges — Array of Delauney edge tables.

13656.content: voronoi.get_edges(diagram: userdata): table Returns every diagram edge. Each edge contains sites, pos, and vertices. sites contains two 1-based input indices, with 0 denoting the clipping boundary. pos contains two { x, y } endpoints. vertices contains two 1-based indices into get_vertices(), with 0 denoting an invalid endpoint. diagram — Generated diagram context. edges — Array of edge tables. ⚠️ 1-based; passed to voronoi unchanged.

13657.content: voronoi.get_num_sites(diagram: userdata): number Returns diagram.numsites, the number of unique generated sites. This may be smaller than the input count when points are duplicated. diagram — Generated diagram context. count — Number of unique generated sites.

13658.content: voronoi.get_num_vertices(diagram: userdata): number Returns diagram.numvertices, the number of unique Voronoi vertices. diagram — Generated diagram context. count — Number of unique vertices.

13659.content: voronoi.get_site(diagram: userdata, index: number): table Returns the generated site for a 1-based original input index. The site has the same fields as entries returned by get_sites(). diagram — Generated diagram context. index — 1-based original input point index. ⚠️ 1-based; passed to voronoi unchanged. site — Site table for the requested input point.

13660.content: voronoi.get_sites(diagram: userdata): table Returns every generated site. A site contains p, index, boundary, edges, and the convenience field area. The p field is { x, y }; index is the 1-based original input index; boundary reports whether the cell touches the clipping boundary; and edges contains counter-clockwise edge tables. diagram — Generated diagram context. sites — Array of site tables. ⚠️ 1-based; passed to voronoi unchanged.

13661.content: voronoi.get_vertices(diagram: userdata): table Returns all unique Voronoi vertices as { x, y } point tables. Edge vertex indices refer to this array. diagram — Generated diagram context. vertices — Array of point tables.

13662.content: voronoi.relax(diagram: userdata) Moves every input point toward the average of its site and cell vertices, then regenerates the diagram. diagram — Generated diagram context.

15211.content: get_device_tier(): "low" | "medium" | "high" | "unknown" Returns the player's device tier. ?deviceTier= set to low, medium, high or unknown wins; next comes the host's window.minit.deviceTier when it is one of the four; otherwise it returns "unknown", which is also its result outside an HTML5 build.

15212.content: get_motion_quality(): "full" | "reduced" Returns the effects quality to run at. ?motionQuality=full or ?motionQuality=reduced wins; next comes the host's window.minit.motionQuality when it is one of the two; otherwise it returns "reduced" when prefers_reduced_motion returns true, else "full". Outside an HTML5 build it returns "full".

15213.content: get_user_data(): string | undefined Returns this player's single stored slot, which report_result writes through its user_data option. Reads the host's window.minit.userData, else the ?userData= URL parameter when the host injected none, else returns undefined. A stored empty value returns "", distinct from undefined. Outside an HTML5 build it returns undefined.

15214.content: is_viewable(): boolean Returns whether the game is visible to the player right now: the host's window.minit.isViewable() when it has one, else whether document.visibilityState is visible. It reads the value again on every call. Outside an HTML5 build it returns true.

15215.content: loading_done() Signals the host that the game is booted and ready to show. The host keeps the game hidden until this is called. Outside an HTML5 build it prints loadingDone.

15216.content: on_viewable_change(fn: (viewable: boolean) => void): () => void Calls fn each time the game's viewability changes, starting from its value at subscribe time, and returns a function that unsubscribes fn. Lua polls the value every 0.25 s, so a change arrives up to about 250 ms late. Subscribing the same fn again returns its existing unsubscribe, and unsubscribing twice is safe. An error fn raises is printed and does not stop the other subscribers. The poll runs on a timer that belongs to the script that subscribed last and stops with it, so subscribe from a script that outlives the subscription and unsubscribe in its final. Outside an HTML5 build fn is never called and the returned function does nothing. fn — Gets true when the game becomes viewable and false when it stops.

15217.content: prefers_reduced_motion(): boolean Returns whether the player or the operating system prefers reduced motion. ?reducedMotion=1 or ?reducedMotion=true forces true and ?reducedMotion=0 or ?reducedMotion=false forces false; next comes the host's window.minit.prefersReducedMotion when it is a boolean; otherwise it returns whether the browser matches the prefers-reduced-motion: reduce media query, or false when the browser cannot tell. Outside an HTML5 build it returns false.

15218.content: report_result(score: number | string, options?: ReportResultOptions) Submits the game's final result. Call it exactly once, when the game ends: the host ignores a repeat call, and the SDK warns about it. A higher score ranks better by default. For a time-sorted game (resultSorting fastestTime or slowestTime in meta.json) the score is in seconds, never milliseconds, and fractions are allowed. Outside an HTML5 build it prints the score. score — The result, as a number or a string. options — The caption, delay and stored slot to send with the result.

15219.content: delay?: number How many milliseconds the host waits before showing the result screen.

15220.content: flavor_text?: string A short caption for the host's result screen and feed. Past 64 characters, counted as a JS string so an emoji counts 2, the SDK warns and the platform cuts it to 64.

15221.content: user_data?: string Writes this player's single stored slot, which get_user_data reads back. Omit it to leave the slot unchanged; "" is a valid write.

15222.content: should_show_tutorial(): boolean Returns whether to run the first-play tutorial. ?tutorial=1 or ?tutorial=true forces it on and ?tutorial=0 or ?tutorial=false forces it off; otherwise it returns false only when the host reports that the player has played the game before. Outside an HTML5 build it returns true.

Ownership of the buffer is not transferred. options — Optional video settings. loop loops the video. format is "rgb" (default, frames converted to RGB on the CPU) or "yuv" (packed YUV planes for the video_yuv shader). decode_ahead (AV1, default true) decodes on a worker thread into a queue. threads (AV1) sets the decoder threads, by default 1 up to 1080p, 2 up to 1440p and 4 above. audio (MPEG1) makes this decoder decode the audio track too, but the samples are not played - use decode_audio() and a sound component for sound. handle — Returns video handle. 15339.content: Morgerion / defold-rtcapture rtcapture Capture of arbitrary render targets and of the default framebuffer. Reads COLOR0 of a render target given by a render script, or the screen itself, and returns raw RGB8/RGBA8 pixels as a Defold buffer, or a PNG or JPEG in memory or written to a file. Binding and readback use the portable DMSDK graphics API only, with no backend specific code.

15340.content: rtcapture.cancel_all(): number Drop every pending capture request. No callbacks are invoked. count — How many requests were dropped.

15341.content: rtcapture.cancel(request_id: number): boolean Drop a pending capture request. Its callback is never invoked, because cancelling was the caller's own decision. Everything the request owned is released immediately. request_id — The id returned by capture. cancelled — True when a pending request with that id was found and removed.

15342.content: rtcapture.capture_sync(target: number, options: table): LuaMultiReturn<[table, string, string]> Read the given target immediately instead of waiting for post render. Takes the same options as capture and returns the same result table, only as a direct return value. Use it where no further post render will happen - the save written from the final() of a game script when the window is closing is the case this exists for, since a queued request there would never run. A render target still has to be captured from the render script that owns it and in the frame it was drawn; the screen framebuffer can be captured from anywhere. target — The value returned by render.render_target(), or rtcapture.RENDER_TARGET_DEFAULT. options — The same options capture accepts. result — The same result table capture passes to its callback, or nil when the request was rejected outright. error — Error code when the request was rejected, otherwise nil. message — Human readable reason when the request was rejected, otherwise nil.

15343.content: rtcapture.capture(target: number, options: table, callback: function): LuaMultiReturn<[number, string, string]> Queue a readback of the given render target. The readback runs in the post-render phase of the current frame, so call this from the render script that owns the target and in the same frame the target was drawn. The extension does not own the target and cannot detect that it was deleted or resized after the request. target — The value returned by render.render_target(), or rtcapture.RENDER_TARGET_DEFAULT for the main screen framebuffer. The screen can be captured from any script; a render target must come from the render script that owns it. options — format - "raw" (default) for pixels in a Defold buffer, "hold" to keep the pixels inside the extension and get a frame_id for encode, "png" or "jpeg". Use "hold" to spread a capture over two frames: the frame that reads pays for the readback only, and the downscale and the encoding happen on the next frame, without a multi megabyte buffer travelling through Lua in between. max_width - target width of the resulting image. The extension picks the integer box filter factor itself, because only it knows the size of the region it read. Rounding is down, with a minimum of 1, so the result can be slightly wider than asked: 3840 with max_width = 600 gives 640. Without this option the image keeps the size of the region that was read. path - encoded formats only. When given, the image is written to that file and is not copied into a Lua string. The file is written through path .. ".tmp" and only then replaces the destination. channels - 4 for RGBA8 or 3 for RGB8 with alpha discarded. Defaults to 4, or to 3 for JPEG, which cannot store alpha anyway. PNG keeps alpha losslessly for four channels and writes a true 24bpp PNG for three. quality - JPEG only, 1..100, default 85. subsampling - JPEG only, "444", "422" or "420", default "420". Use "444" for text and interface, where chroma subsampling produces coloured fringes. progressive - JPEG only, default false. Encodes noticeably slower and decodes slower, with little size benefit for local previews. optimize - JPEG only, default false. Optimized Huffman tables cost encoding time. alpha_mode - JPEG from four channels. "discard" (default) ignores alpha, so transparent areas keep whatever colour they hold. "composite" blends onto background first. background - table with r, g, b in 0..255, used by alpha_mode = "composite". Defaults to black. x, y, width, height - rectangle to read, with the origin in the top left corner of the target, matching the orientation of the returned image. x and y default to 0; width and height default to the rest of the target. A rectangle that leaves the target is rejected, never clamped. flip_y - flip rows vertically, false by default. The default was measured: on the OpenGL adapter ReadPixels already returns top-down rows. tag - any Lua value, returned unchanged in the result so a caller can correlate the result with its own request. callback — Called from post-render with one result table. request_id — Monotonic id of the accepted request, or nil when the request was rejected. error — Error code when the request was rejected, otherwise nil. message — Human readable reason when the request was rejected, otherwise nil.

15344.content: rtcapture.debug_target(target: number, label?: string): table Identify an arbitrary render target without reading its pixels. Call it from the render script that owns the target, in the same frame, so the handle is guaranteed to be alive. target — The value returned by render.render_target(). label — Name used in the log line so several targets can be told apart. info — Contains label, handle, handle_hex, color0_width, color0_height and adapter.

15345.content: rtcapture.decode_jpeg(data: string, options?: table): LuaMultiReturn<[table, string, string]> Decode JPEG bytes into a Defold buffer. Synchronous, and callable from any script. The header is validated before anything is allocated dimensions, data precision and colour space are checked first, and images above 64 million pixels are refused. JPEG stores no alpha, so a four channel result is always fully opaque. data — Binary JPEG data. options — channels - 4 for RGBA8 (default) or 3 for RGB8. image — Contains width, height, channels, byte_size, decode_ms and buffer, a Defold buffer whose single stream is rgba of UINT8 x4, or rgb of UINT8 x3. nil when decoding failed. error — Error code when decoding failed, otherwise nil. message — Human readable reason when decoding failed, otherwise nil.

15346.content: rtcapture.encode(frame_id: number, options: table): LuaMultiReturn<[table, string, string]> Downscale and encode a frame that a format = "hold" capture left inside the extension. This is the second phase of a capture spread over two frames. The frame stays held after encoding, so the same shot can be encoded more than once - to compare formats, for example - and is freed by release_frame. Compositing is not available here the held pixels have already been converted, so alpha_mode = "composite" only works at capture time. frame_id — The frame_id from the result of the held capture. options — format (required, "png" or "jpeg"), path, max_width, quality, subsampling, progressive, optimize and tag - the same meaning they have in capture. result — The same result table shape as capture, with downscale_ms, encode_ms, write_ms and total_ms filled for this phase. nil when the call was rejected. error — ERR_NO_HELD_FRAME when no frame with that id is held, otherwise nil. message — Human readable reason when the call was rejected, otherwise nil.

15347.content: rtcapture.get_capabilities(): table Report what the extension can currently do on the installed graphics adapter. Only verified capabilities are listed; stages that are not implemented yet do not appear as fields. capabilities — Contains available, adapter ("opengl", "vulkan", "directx", ...) and debug_target.

15348.content: rtcapture.get_render_target_size(target: number): LuaMultiReturn<[number, number]> Report the size of the COLOR0 attachment of the given render target, so calling code can compute a rectangle without repeating the parameters the render script created the target with. target — The value returned by render.render_target().

15349.content: rtcapture.invalidate_render_targets(): number Declare that every render target handed to the extension so far is gone. Call this right after recreating render targets, for example when the window was resized. The extension cannot detect this on its own - the public DMSDK has no way to test whether a handle is still alive. Requests made before the call stay in the queue and complete with ERR_RENDER_TARGET_DESTROYED rather than reading through a dead handle, so every accepted request still gets exactly one answer. Requests for rtcapture.RENDER_TARGET_DEFAULT are unaffected. affected — How many pending requests will now fail.

15350.content: rtcapture.release_frame(frame_id?: number): boolean Free the frame held by a format = "hold" capture. Call it once the frame has been encoded, or when the encoding is abandoned - otherwise a full screen frame stays in the memory of the extension until the next held capture replaces it. Only one frame is held at a time. frame_id — The id to free. Without it the currently held frame is freed, whatever its id. released — True when a frame was actually freed.

15351.content: rtcapture.RENDER_TARGET_DEFAULT Pass as the capture target to read the main screen framebuffer instead of a render target. Its value is 0, the same one render.RENDER_TARGET_DEFAULT uses in a render script.

15352.content: rtcapture.set_debug_logging(enabled: boolean) Enable the detailed capture log. Off by default. The log line reports the raw first pixel before conversion, the viewport before and after the readback, and per stage timings.

15634.content: compute(node: Flow_Element, x: number, y: number, w: number, h: number) Compute layout for a node tree. Writes layout.x/y/w/h to every node in the tree recursively, using bottom-left origin coordinates. Algorithm: 1. Measure all regular (non-overlay) children to sum fixed sizes and flex_grow weights. 2. Distribute remaining free space according to justify_content. 3. Place each child along the main axis, applying align_items / align_self on the cross axis. 4. Recurse into each child. 5. Layout overlay children (popup, bottom_sheet) at full parent bounds as a final pass. node — The root element to compute layout for x — Left edge of the available area in layout space (px) y — Bottom edge of the available area in layout space (px) w — Available width in pixels h — Available height in pixels

15645.content: build_tree(adapter: LuaTable): Flow_Element | undefined Build (or rebuild) the UI element tree for the current navigation state. When a transition is active, renders both from and to trees and applies alpha or offset_x according to the transition type and eased progress. Transition types: "fade" — cross-fade: from_tree.alpha fades out, to_tree.alpha fades in "slide_left" — to slides in from the right: from moves left, to comes from right "slide_right" — to slides in from the left: from moves right, to comes from left Returns nil and clears adapter.tree when the stack is empty. adapter — The adapter instance The UI tree to pass to the renderer

Coordinates must be in GUI space (as received from on_input action.x/y). Returns the deepest hittable element whose layout bounds contain the point, or nil if nothing was hit. self — The gui_script self table with a mounted renderer x — X coordinate in GUI space y — Y coordinate in GUI space The hit element, or nil
