16232.content: on_input(self: LuaMap<string, unknown> | PlainTable, action_id: Hash | undefined, action: { x?: number; y?: number; pressed?: boolean; released?: boolean }): boolean Route a Defold input action to the appropriate element. Handles touch press/move/release, scroll wheel, and drag gestures. Call this from gui_script on_input(); returns true if the input was consumed. self — The gui_script self table with a mounted renderer action_id — The Defold action id hash (e.g. hash("touch")) action — The Defold action table with x, y, pressed, released fields True if the input was consumed and should not propagate

16233.content: register(type_name: string, def: LuaTable): LuaTable Register a custom element type definition. Every element type string ("box", "text", "button", etc.) must be registered before it can appear in a UI tree. The definition describes how to create, update, and interact with the corresponding Defold GUI node. Required fields in def: create_node(el) -> userdata — creates and returns a new gui node Optional fields in def: apply(self, el, node, alpha) — update node visuals each frame is_visible(el) -> boolean — custom visibility check is_hittable(el) -> boolean — custom hit-test eligibility is_scroll_container -> boolean — marks element as scroll root clips_children -> boolean — node is used as parent for children capture_descendant_hits -> boolean — returns self instead of child on hit is_backdrop_click_target -> boolean — receives backdrop click events get_text_anchor(el) -> "left"|"center"|"right" — text pivot anchor for positioning hover_begin(self, el, deps) — called when pointer enters element hover_end(self, el, deps) — called when pointer leaves element press_begin(self, el, deps) — called when element is pressed press_update(self, el, is_hot, deps) — called while dragging over element press_end(self, el, activated, deps) — called on release on_wheel(self, el, delta, deps) — called on mouse wheel on_drag_start(self, el, x, y, t, deps) — called when drag begins on_drag_move(self, el, x, y, t, deps) — called each drag frame on_drag_end(self, el, action, t, deps) — called when drag ends update_anim(el, dt, deps) -> bool,bool — per-frame animation tick render_extras(self, el, prefix, alpha, deps) — render auxiliary nodes collect_extra_keys(el, prefix, keys, deps) — declare extra cached node keys get_child_extra_offset_y(el) -> number — additional Y offset for children type_name — The element type string (e.g. "box", "scroll") def — Renderer definition table; must contain create_node The registered def, same reference as the argument

Cheaper than M.update() — no redraw-flag check, just a size comparison. Returns true when a re-render was performed. self — The gui_script self table with a mounted renderer tree — The element tree to render; falls back to self.ui.tree True if a re-render was performed

16235.content: render(self: LuaMap<string, unknown> | PlainTable, tree: Flow_Element, w?: number | undefined, h?: number | undefined) Force a full layout + render pass using the given tree and dimensions. Bypasses redraw gating — always re-computes and re-applies all nodes. Prefer M.update() for normal frame rendering; use M.render() when you need to guarantee an immediate re-render (e.g. after a window resize event detected in on_input). self — The gui_script self table with a mounted renderer tree — The element tree to render w — Available width in pixels (nil/0 = use GUI size) h — Available height in pixels (nil/0 = use GUI size)

16239.content: update_animations(self: LuaMap<string, unknown> | PlainTable, dt: number): boolean ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- Advance all per-element animations by one frame (dt seconds). 16308.content: paweljarosz / defold-fake-real-glass fake_real_glass A multipass glass rendering library for Defold with screen-space double refraction, thickness-based distortion, optional color absorption and local cubemap reflection probes. Supports lighting from Defold light components and configurable reflection modes that update probes every frame, capture once or use pre-rendered cubemaps. Includes a reusable Lua render module, glass materials and example scenes with glass spheres, a wine glass and planar mirror reflections. Integrates with custom render pipelines and requires Defold 1.14.0 or newer. Register node templates once with registerTemplates, create a tree over a payload with new, and call run: each node moves on only when the one before it reports success or failure, and a tree can start from any node id, so an active node saved with a game can be resumed on load. new

(config: { tree_name: string; payload: P; rng?: (this: void, range_start: number, range_end: number) => number; }): BehaviorTree

Creates a tree that runs a registered tree template over a payload. Register the templates with registerTemplates first. config — tree_name names a tree under the templates' TREES, payload is passed to every task callback, and rng returns a whole number between its two arguments for Random and RandomWithChances; it defaults to math.random. new(config: { tree_name: string; payload?: undefined; rng?: (this: void, range_start: number, range_end: number) => number; }): BehaviorTree Creates a tree that runs a registered tree template with no payload, so its task callbacks receive undefined. 18239.content: astar.setup(map_width: number, map_height: number, direction: number, allocate: number, typical_adjacent: number, cache[optional]: boolean, use_zero[optional]: boolean, map_vflip[optional]: boolean, map_id[optional]: number) Initial setup. You have to setup the astar before calling any other methods. map_width — Width of your map. This is generally width of your tilemap. map_height — Height of your map. This is generally width of your tilemap. direction — Movement direction (astar.DIRECTION_FOUR or astar.DIRECTION_EIGHT) astar.DIRECTION_FOUR - on a square grid that allows 4 directions of movement using Manhattan distance. astar.DIRECTION_EIGHT - on a square grid that allows 8 directions of movement using Euclidean distance. allocate — How many states should be internally allocated at a time. This can be hard to get correct. The higher the value, the more memory Patfinder will use. If you have a small map (a few thousand states?) it may make sense to pass in the maximum value. This will cache everything, and MicroPather will only need one main memory allocation. For a chess board, allocate would be set to 8x8 (64) If your map is large, something like 1/4 the number of possible states is good. If your state space is huge, use a multiple (5-10x) of the normal path. "Occasionally" call astar.reset_cache() to free unused memory. typical_adjacent — Used to determine cache size. The typical number of adjacent states to a given state. (On a chessboard, 8.) Higher values use a little more memory. cache[optional] — Turn on path caching. Uses more memory (yet again) but at a huge speed advantage if you may call the pather with the same path or sub-path, which is common for pathing over maps in games. Default is true use_zero[optional] — Toggle start index 0 or 1 for tables and tile positions. Also you can set it by call astar.use_zero(). Default is false map_vflip[optional] — Flips the map vertically. This doesn't flip the coordinates. Also you can set it by call astar.map_vflip(). Default is false map_id[optional] — ID of the map. Has to be an integer from 0 to 2^16 - 1. Default is 0.

18537.content: selimanac / defold-stylized-water-shader water A stylized water shader: animated wave surfaces, foam, sparkles, refraction and reflection, set through shader constants. A game object script calls init once with the camera, sun and water objects, then update(dt) and update_camera() every frame. The render script calls render_init(self) at the end of its init, after which self.predicates holds the water predicate, and render_update(self, state, self.predicates, draw_options_world) in its update (see water/render/water.render_script). The shader needs exclude_gles_sm100 = 1 under [shader] in game.project. Every setter writes a shader constant the next render_update uploads, and every getter returns the stored values as separate values. RenderScriptSelf Predicates RenderState

18572.content: set_deep_color(r: number, g: number, b: number) Sets the water color in deep areas. r — The red component, 0 to 1. g — The green component, 0 to 1. b — The blue component, 0 to 1.

18573.content: set_density_params(distance_density: number, depth_density: number) Sets how the color fades with distance and blends with depth. distance_density — How quickly the color fades to the far color: 0.01 very slow, 0.1 normal, 0.5 quick. depth_density — How quickly the color moves from the shallow color to the deep color with water depth.

18574.content: set_edge_foam_color(r: number, g: number, b: number) Sets the edge foam color. r — The red component, 0 to 1. g — The green component, 0 to 1. b — The blue component, 0 to 1.

18575.content: set_edge_foam_params(depth_scale: number, noise_strength: number, edge_softness: number, alpha: number) Sets the foam drawn where the water meets other geometry, based on water depth. depth_scale — How quickly the foam fades with depth; lower values give more foam. noise_strength — The noise distortion strength, about 0.2 to 0.5. edge_softness — The edge blend softness, about 0.02 to 0.15. alpha — The overall foam opacity, 0 to 1.

18576.content: set_edge_foam_type(type: 0 | 1) Sets how the edge foam is drawn. It also prints SET and the type on every call. type — 0 draws a solid color, 1 a texture.

18577.content: set_far_color(r: number, g: number, b: number) Sets the water color far from the camera, which the surface fades to with distance. r — The red component, 0 to 1. g — The green component, 0 to 1. b — The blue component, 0 to 1.

18578.content: set_foam_params(scale: number, speed: number, noise_scale: number, contribution: number) Sets the foam's look and animation. scale — The foam texture tiling; lower values give bigger foam patches. speed — The animation speed. noise_scale — The normal map distortion: 0 none, 0.5 moderate, 1 heavy. contribution — The overall foam visibility: 0 no foam, 0.5 subtle, 1 full.

18579.content: set_lod_params(sparkle_distance: number, foam_distance: number) Sets the level-of-detail distances beyond which effects are simplified. sparkle_distance — The distance beyond which sparkles are skipped, saving eight texture samples, 0 to 500. The default is 100. foam_distance — The distance beyond which a simplified foam is drawn, saving three texture samples, 0 to 500. The default is 150.

18580.content: set_reflection_params(strength: number, fresnel_power?: number) Sets the cubemap reflection. The reflection samples the cubemap bound to the water material's reflection_cubemap sampler; this module binds none. strength — The reflection intensity: 0 off, 0.5 moderate, 1 strong. fresnel_power — How much stronger the reflection is at grazing angles, 1 to 5: 1 the same at every angle, 3 natural, 5 very strong. Defaults to 3.

18581.content: set_refraction_params(strength: number, chromatic_aberration?: number) Sets the screen-space refraction. strength — The refraction intensity: 0 off, 0.5 moderate, 1 strong. chromatic_aberration — The color separation: 0 off, 0.5 subtle, 1 strong. Defaults to 0.

18582.content: set_shallow_color(r: number, g: number, b: number) Sets the water color in shallow areas. The shader always uses an alpha of 1. r — The red component, 0 to 1. g — The green component, 0 to 1. b — The blue component, 0 to 1.

18583.content: set_skybox_cubemap(cubemap_path: string) Prints a warning and does nothing else. cubemap_path — The cubemap texture path, for example /main/skybox.cubemap.

18584.content: set_sparkle_color(r: number, g: number, b: number) Sets the sparkle tint color. r — The red component, 0 to 1. g — The green component, 0 to 1. b — The blue component, 0 to 1.

18585.content: set_sparkle_params(scale: number, speed: number, exponent: number, enabled?: number) Sets the sparkle (glitter) effect. scale — The sparkle texture tiling. speed — The animation speed. exponent — The sharpness: 1000 many soft sparkles, 10000 medium, 100000 very few, very sharp ones. enabled — 0 disables sparkles and 1 enables them. When omitted, the current value is kept.

18586.content: set_sun_color(r: number, g: number, b: number) Sets the sun light color. r — The red component, 0 to 1. g — The green component, 0 to 1. b — The blue component, 0 to 1.

18587.content: set_sun_direction(x: number, y: number, z: number) Sets the directional light direction. init and update_sun overwrite it with the direction from the water object to the sun. x — The X component of the normalized direction. y — The Y component of the normalized direction. z — The Z component of the normalized direction.

18588.content: set_sun_params(exponent: number) Sets the sharpness of the sun's specular highlight. exponent — The highlight sharpness: 100 big and soft, 1000 medium, 10000 tiny and sharp.

18589.content: set_wave_normal_params(scale: number, speed: number) Sets the animated normal map that adds ripple detail to the surface. scale — The normal map tiling: 5 large ripples, 10 medium, 20 tiny. speed — The animation speed: 0.5 slow, 1 normal, 2 fast.

18590.content: set_wave1(direction: number, amplitude: number, wavelength: number, speed: number) Sets the first wave layer. direction — The wave direction in radians, 0 to 2π: 0 east, π/2 north, π west, 3π/2 south. amplitude — The wave height: 0.1 to 0.5 gentle, 0.5 to 1 medium, 1 to 2 rough, above 2 a storm. wavelength — The distance between wave peaks: 10 to 20 choppy, 20 to 40 ocean waves, above 40 long gentle swells. speed — The animation speed: 0.5 to 1 slow, 1 to 3 moderate, 3 to 5 fast, above 5 very fast.

18591.content: set_wave2(direction: number, amplitude: number, wavelength: number, speed: number) Sets the second wave layer, with the same ranges as set_wave1. direction — The wave direction in radians, 0 to 2π. amplitude — The wave height: 0.1 to 0.5 gentle, 0.5 to 1 medium, 1 to 2 rough, above 2 a storm. wavelength — The distance between wave peaks: 10 to 20 choppy, 20 to 40 ocean waves, above 40 long gentle swells. speed — The animation speed: 0.5 to 1 slow, 1 to 3 moderate, 3 to 5 fast, above 5 very fast.

18592.content: update_camera() Re-reads the camera world position and its near and far Z planes. Call it every frame.

18593.content: update_sun() Re-reads the sun position, which moves the light and recomputes the sun direction from the water object, replacing any direction set_sun_direction wrote.

18594.content: update(dt: number) Advances the wave time by dt times the time speed init stored, unless the timer is paused. Call it every frame. dt — The frame time in seconds.

18605.content: selimanac / defold-tile-raycast tile_raycast Ray Casting in tiled worlds using DDA algorithm.

18606.content: BOTTOM: number The ray hit the bottom side of the tile.

18607.content: cast(from_x: number, from_y: number, to_x: number, to_y: number): LuaMultiReturn<[ false ] | [ true, number, number, number, number, number, number, number ]> Casts a ray through the tile map and reports the first target tile it hits. A miss returns false alone, so check hit before reading the other values. Before setup, it logs an error and returns nothing. from_x — X coordinate of the ray start. from_y — Y coordinate of the ray start. to_x — X coordinate of the ray end. to_y — Y coordinate of the ray end. hit, then on a hit: tile_x, tile_y, array_id (index in the tile table), tile_id, intersection_x, intersection_y and side (LEFT, RIGHT, TOP or BOTTOM). ⚠️ tile_x is 1-based; passed to tile_raycast unchanged. ⚠️ tile_y is 1-based; passed to tile_raycast unchanged. ⚠️ array_id is 1-based; passed to tile_raycast unchanged.

18608.content: get_at(tile_x: number, tile_y: number, tile_id: number) Sets the tile ID at a tile coordinate. The extension registers its writer under this name and its reader as {@link tile_raycast.set_at}, the reverse of what its documentation describes. tile_x — Tile X coordinate. ⚠️ 1-based; passed to tile_raycast unchanged. tile_y — Tile Y coordinate. ⚠️ 1-based; passed to tile_raycast unchanged. tile_id — Tile ID to set.

18609.content: LEFT: number The ray hit the left side of the tile.

18610.content: reset() Clears all tile and tile map data.

18611.content: RIGHT: number The ray hit the right side of the tile.

18612.content: set_at(tile_x: number, tile_y: number): number Returns the tile ID at a tile coordinate. The extension registers its reader under this name and its writer as {@link tile_raycast.get_at}, the reverse of what its documentation describes. tile_x — Tile X coordinate. ⚠️ 1-based; passed to tile_raycast unchanged. tile_y — Tile Y coordinate. ⚠️ 1-based; passed to tile_raycast unchanged. The tile ID at that coordinate.

18613.content: setup(tile_width: number, tile_height: number, tilemap_width: number, tilemap_height: number, tiles: number[], target_tiles: number[]) Sets up the tile map to cast rays through, replacing any previous one. tile_width — Width of a single tile. tile_height — Height of a single tile. tilemap_width — Number of tiles horizontally in the tile map. tilemap_height — Number of tiles vertically in the tile map. tiles — One-dimensional table of tile IDs, row by row. target_tiles — IDs of the tiles a ray stops at, such as walls.

18614.content: TOP: number The ray hit the top side of the tile.

18632.content: selimanac / defold-wave wave Wave simulation that floats, pitches and rolls game objects on a water surface.

18633.content: add_gameobject(instance: SceneGameObjectAddress | Hash | Url, float_offset: number, water_base_y: number, sample_distance: number, rotation_smoothing?: number, use_world_transform?: boolean, forward?: Vector3): number Add a floating game object to the wave simulation. The model must face -Z in its unrotated state: wave sampling, pitch, roll and movement all assume it. To face another way at runtime, call set_yaw after registration, or pass the matching forward. instance — The game object. float_offset — Vertical offset from the water surface. water_base_y — Y coordinate of the flat water plane. sample_distance — Probe offset used to compute the pitch and roll normals. rotation_smoothing — SLERP factor: 0 or omitted disables rotation, 1 snaps instantly. use_world_transform — true for objects nested under another moving object, false for root objects. forward — World-space direction the model's nose faces at registration. Default is vmath.vector3(0, 0, -1). The floater ID used by every later call, or 0 on error such as exceeded capacity.

18634.content: get_wave1_height(pos_x: number, pos_z: number, time: number): number Sample the wave 1 height at a world position, at the simulation's current time. pos_x — World X. pos_z — World Z. time — Required by the runtime; the sample uses the simulation's own clock instead. The wave height.

18635.content: get_wave2_height(pos_x: number, pos_z: number, time: number): number Sample the wave 2 height at a world position, at the simulation's current time. pos_x — World X. pos_z — World Z. time — Required by the runtime; the sample uses the simulation's own clock instead. The wave height.

18636.content: init(wave1_direction: number, wave1_amplitude: number, wave1_wavelength: number, wave1_speed: number, wave2_direction: number, wave2_amplitude: number, wave2_wavelength: number, wave2_speed: number, time_speed: number, gameobject_capacity: number) Initialize the wave simulation. Call it once before any other wave function, with the same parameters the water shader uses. wave1_direction — Wave 1 direction (0.0 to 2.0, multiplied by π internally). wave1_amplitude — Wave 1 height in world units. wave1_wavelength — Wave 1 distance between peaks. wave1_speed — Wave 1 animation speed. wave2_direction — Wave 2 direction (0.0 to 2.0). wave2_amplitude — Wave 2 height in world units. wave2_wavelength — Wave 2 distance between peaks. wave2_speed — Wave 2 animation speed. time_speed — Global time multiplier. gameobject_capacity — Pre-allocated entity table size (for example 256), fixed at init time.

18637.content: is_pause(): boolean Whether the wave update loop is paused. true when paused.

18638.content: move(id: number, max_speed: number, speed_factor: number) Begin moving a floater forward at up to max_speed, accelerating by speed_factor per second. id — Floater ID. max_speed — Target and maximum speed in world units per second. speed_factor — Acceleration factor; higher ramps up faster.

18639.content: pause(state: boolean) Pause or resume the wave update loop without removing entities. state — true to pause, false to resume.

18640.content: set_yaw(id: number, yaw: number) Override the yaw (heading) of a floater, for steering such as a boat turning. id — Floater ID. yaw — Yaw in radians.

18641.content: shutdown() Shut down the wave simulation and free all resources. The extension finalizer calls it automatically; call it yourself only to reinitialize.

18642.content: stop(id: number) Stop a floater. Its target speed becomes 0 and it decelerates smoothly by its speed factor. id — Floater ID.

18643.content: update_wave1(direction: number, amplitude: number, wavelength: number, speed: number) Live-update the wave 1 parameters. Call it in sync with the water shader's wave 1 update to keep visuals and physics aligned. direction — Wave direction. amplitude — Wave height. wavelength — Distance between peaks. speed — Animation speed.

18644.content: update_wave2(direction: number, amplitude: number, wavelength: number, speed: number) Live-update the wave 2 parameters. Call it in sync with the water shader's wave 2 update to keep visuals and physics aligned. direction — Wave direction. amplitude — Wave height. wavelength — Distance between peaks. speed — Animation speed.

19012.content: tocaRepo / defold-androidextension-ump ump Google User Messaging Platform consent API for Android. The table is absent on other platforms.

19013.content: ump.can_request_ads(): boolean UMP ad-request eligibility. Check after the current update callback. Before then, this can reflect consent stored from an earlier session. allowed — True when UMP allows ad requests.

19014.content: ump.GDPR_APPLIES_NO 0; IAB TCF value says GDPR does not apply.

19015.content: ump.GDPR_APPLIES_UNKNOWN -1; IAB TCF GDPR applicability value missing or invalid.

19016.content: ump.GDPR_APPLIES_YES 1; IAB TCF value says GDPR applies.

19017.content: ump.get_consent_status(): number Google consent status: 0 unknown, 1 not required, 2 required, 3 obtained. Returns -1 before the consent-information object exists. Status 3 does not distinguish personalized from non-personalized advertising. status — UMP consent status or -1 if unavailable.

19018.content: ump.get_gdpr_applies(): number Read IABTCF_gdprApplies from Android default preferences after a successful UMP update. This is a GDPR applicability signal, not a country code or vendor consent. value — ump.GDPR_APPLIES_NO, ump.GDPR_APPLIES_YES, or ump.GDPR_APPLIES_UNKNOWN if missing or invalid.

19019.content: ump.get_privacy_options_state(): number Diagnostic state of the latest privacy-options form. state — One of ump.PRIVACY_OPTIONS_STATE_NOT_SHOWN, ump.PRIVACY_OPTIONS_STATE_SHOWING, ump.PRIVACY_OPTIONS_STATE_DISMISSED, or ump.PRIVACY_OPTIONS_STATE_ERROR.

19020.content: ump.get_purpose_consents(): string Read the raw IABTCF_PurposeConsents bit string from Android default preferences. Call after a successful UMP update or privacy-options callback. The third character represents TCF Purpose 3 consent. value — Raw purpose-consent bit string, or nil if unavailable.

19021.content: ump.get_request_state(): number Diagnostic state of the latest consent information update and form. Prefer the request callback to polling this value. state — One of ump.REQUEST_STATE_UPDATING, ump.REQUEST_STATE_FORM_PENDING, ump.REQUEST_STATE_COMPLETE, or ump.REQUEST_STATE_FAILED.

19022.content: ump.initialize_mobile_ads_sdk() Legacy, nonfunctional export. Its required Java method is absent from this extension. Do not call it. If using the Defold AdMob extension, call admob.initialize() after the UMP flow instead.

19023.content: ump.is_privacy_options_required(): boolean Whether UMP requires a privacy-options entry point. Returns false before consent information is available. required — True when a privacy-options entry point is required.

19024.content: ump.PRIVACY_OPTIONS_STATE_DISMISSED 2; privacy-options form closed without a UMP error.

19028.content: ump.request_consent_info_update(test_device: boolean, test_device_hashed_id: string, callback?: function, defer_form?: boolean) Request fresh consent information and show a consent form if required. Call on every launch. The callback runs on the Defold update thread after the update and any required form finish unless defer_form is true. In deferred mode the callback runs after the information update, before any form opens; call show_consent_form_if_required to finish the flow. A successful callback means no UMP error, not consent to personalized ads. test_device — Enable UMP debug mode and force EEA geography for the registered test device. test_device_hashed_id — Hashed test device ID. Pass an empty string when test_device is false. callback — Called when the update and any required form finish. defer_form — Pause after the information update so an application notice can precede a required form. Defaults to false.

19029.content: ump.REQUEST_STATE_COMPLETE 1; update and form step finished without a UMP error.

19030.content: ump.REQUEST_STATE_FAILED 2; information update or form failed.

19031.content: ump.REQUEST_STATE_FORM_PENDING 3; update succeeded and the form step is waiting or in progress.

19032.content: ump.REQUEST_STATE_UPDATING 0; initial state or consent information update in progress.

19033.content: ump.reset_consent_information() Clear UMP consent information for testing if its object has been created. Start a new request afterward. Diagnostic request/form states are not reset by this call.

19034.content: ump.show_consent_form_if_required(callback?: function) Continue a successful deferred consent-information update. Check was_consent_form_required() to decide whether to show an application notice first. Call only once, after that notice has closed. The callback runs after the required form closes or fails, or immediately if no form is required. Advertising must wait for this callback. callback — Called when the form step finishes.

19035.content: ump.show_privacy_options_form(callback?: function) Open the UMP privacy-options form in response to user input. Check is_privacy_options_required() first. A successful callback means the form closed without an error, not that the user granted consent. callback — Called after the privacy-options form is dismissed or fails.

19036.content: ump.was_consent_form_required(): boolean Whether the latest successful information update found a required normal consent form. Resets when a new update starts. May remain true if that form later fails. required — True if the latest successful update required a form.

A project reaches it as client.http, and every asobi.api. module sends through it. HttpError

19903.content: wavedash.EVENT_PURCHASE_COMPLETED Fired once per purchase made while the game is running (in-game paywall, game page, gift, another tab), plus, at launch, once per consumable still unfulfilled. Payload: { purchaseId, contentIdentifier, type, fulfilled, purchasedAt, receiptJwt }. Durables arrive with fulfilled true, already granted. For a consumable, grant it, then call fulfill_purchase_async(purchaseId); until then it's redelivered every launch, so dedupe on purchaseId if you persist grants.

19905.content: wavedash.fulfill_purchase_async(purchase_id: string): function Mark a consumable purchase fulfilled once the grant is saved, so it stops being redelivered. A game's backend can do the same with POST /api/purchases/{purchaseId}/fulfill and the purchase's receiptJwt; both are idempotent, so calling either or both is safe. Resolves with a status in data: FULFILLED, ALREADY_FULFILLED (also success), or NOT_FOUND (unknown or refunded: don't grant it). This is an asynchronous function. The result will be delivered as an event with id 'fulfillPurchase' or as a return value if the function is called from a coroutine. response — Returns { status } in data. (Note: Only if called from within a coroutine)

19906.content: wavedash.FULFILL_PURCHASE_STATUS_ALREADY_FULFILLED fulfill_purchase_async status: also success. The game or its backend fulfilled it earlier, or it's a durable.

19907.content: wavedash.FULFILL_PURCHASE_STATUS_FULFILLED fulfill_purchase_async status: marked fulfilled by this call.

19908.content: wavedash.FULFILL_PURCHASE_STATUS_NOT_FOUND fulfill_purchase_async status: unknown purchase, or it was refunded. Don't grant it.

20124.content: The decision: fork, hand-author, or keep?

20126.content: 1. Add a fork to the library's library.json

20127.content: 2. Vendor the .d.ts and generate the artifacts

20129.content: 4. Surface parity against the upstream Lua

20134.content: Why the two axes are never averaged

20135.content: When a target cannot be measured

20136.content: 5. Cut the library over and validate

20143.content: Some Defold libraries ship no usable structured type source — no .script_api, no inline LuaLS (---@) annotations, and no README that documents the surface precisely enough to parse. The LuaLS, .script_api, and markdown front-ends all ingest a primary source and generate a declaration; a library with none of those has nothing to generate from. Its .d.ts must be written by hand — either forked from an existing hand-authored declaration or authored fresh — and vendored into the library's folder in the toolchain repo as first-party source. resolve then prints the vendored declaration into the consumer's project, the way it prints the generated lanes' declarations. Like the other lanes, adding such a library is data, not code: you add one fork to the library's library.json in its folder, packages/library-types/data/<version>/<host>/<owner>/<repo>/ (the newest version-named folder), vendor the .d.ts into the folder's fork/, run the generation command, and commit the library's files. Every path a fork names is relative to the library folder, except apiDoc and fidelity, which are relative to packages/library-types/, where the tools write their reports. The toolchain's authored front-end (packages/cli/src/library/sync-authored-types.ts) is the reusable machinery; you touch config and fixtures, not the pipeline. This page is for library-type authors. Library data lives in the toolchain repo under packages/library-types/data/, so you add or change a library with a pull request there, not to defold-typescript/library-data. If you only want to use a vendored library in your own game, you need nothing here — just declare the dependency and run resolve. The bun commands on this page run from the toolchain root. Each tool reads and writes the library data under packages/library-types/data/ and writes its reports to api-doc/ and fidelity/ in packages/library-types/.

20144.content: Reach this lane only after ruling out the generated ones. Ask, in order: Does upstream ship a .script_api? → it is a script_api target. Does its Lua carry inline ---@ annotations? → it is a LuaLS target. Does its README document the full surface precisely? → it may be a markdown target (gated on a fidelity comparison; a lossy README is a no-go and the library does not regenerate from markdown). None of the above → it is an authored target, and you choose between fork, hand-author, and keep. A markdown no-go is a verdict on the markdown source, not on the ts-defold dependency. It says the README cannot regenerate the surface; it says nothing about where the surface should be maintained. That second question is this lane's, and a no-go library reaches question 4 with it still open — so run the cost model below on it exactly as you would on a library that never had a README at all. keep is a legitimate answer, but it has to be chosen, not inherited from the refusal. persist.persist and orthographic.camera are the worked examples.

20145.content: An authored .d.ts has no upstream source to regenerate from, so every future upstream API change is a manual edit to the vendored declaration. That is the standing cost. Weigh it against the gain of severing ts-defold: a first-party authored surface is authored-here, carries its own upstream repo/tag pin (not the shared ts-defold/library commit), and is maintained on the toolchain repo's own cadence rather than inherited from a third-party vendoring. Fork — copy the retired ts-defold .d.ts verbatim as the first-party fixture. Zero fidelity risk (the surface is identical to what shipped), and the provenance moves to the real upstream. Best when the ts-defold binding is already correct and the surface is small and stable, so the manual-maintenance cost is low. Hand-author — write a fresh .d.ts from the library's documentation. Only worth it when the ts-defold binding is wrong or absent and the surface is small enough to author confidently. Keep — leave the library ts-defold-sourced. Correct when the surface is large or churns often, so the manual-maintenance cost outweighs the provenance gain, or when a generated lane is likely to become available. Spent for the current corpus: every library the ts-defold registry once carried has severed and library-targets.json holds "targets": [] (see 5. Cut the library over and validate), so a library reaching this decision today has no ts-defold binding to keep — the real choice is fork versus hand-author.

20146.content: Start with library add, which writes the folder, library.json and reviewed.json from the archive URL: Then add the forks entry to library.json by hand, and vendor the upstream Lua it measures against. library add writes no fork, and when it wrote a recipe.json for a generated module, delete that entry and its source/ files if the fork replaces it. Each library sits in its own folder under the data folder, named for its repository: the URL's last path segment, lowercased, without .git (https://github.com/britzl/defcon is defcon/). The folder pins the library's own upstream repository and ref once — an authored library is the sole maintainer of its namespace, so it carries its own repo/ref rather than the shared vendored commit: | File | Field | Required | What it is | | -------------- | ------ | -------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | library.json | repo | yes | The GitHub or Codeberg repository URL, e.g. https://github.com/britzl/defcon. upstream:library-check reads no other host. | | File | Field | Required | What it is | | -------------- | --------- | -------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | library.json | license | no | SPDX-style license id, surfaced by the library page's provenance block. Defaults to "". | | File | Field | Required | What it is | | -------------- | --------- | -------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | library.json | refKind | no | "tag" or "commit" when upstream publishes no stable release (GitHub's latest release skips prereleases), so the docs page's adopt step names the pinned archive instead of linking a releases page. Omit it for a repo with releases. | | File | Field | Required | What it is | | --------------- | ----- | -------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | reviewed.json | ref | yes | The immutable upstream ref to pin. Prefer the newest stable release tag (git ls-remote --tags <repo>) — never invent one. When upstream publishes no tags, pin the current default-branch commit SHA instead; the docs page renders the full SHA as the source ref. | Each forked module is one entry in library.json's forks list: | Field | Required | What it is | | ---------- | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | | authored | yes | Path of the vendored authored/forked .d.ts, relative to the library folder — fork/<moduleId>.d.ts. | | Field | Required | What it is | | ---------- | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | | moduleId | yes | The library's runtime require path, dotted (e.g. defcon.console). This is the declare module name inside the vendored .d.ts. | | Field | Required | What it is | | ----------- | -------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | namespace | yes | The artifact stem — the emitted file is api-doc/<namespace>.json. Either a bare stem (defcon) or the dotted moduleId (orthographic.camera): fork onto the retired module name when it already equals the publish namespace, and reach for a bare stem only when nothing else owns it. The orthographic.camera worked example below settles the choice. | | Field | Required | What it is | | -------- | -------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- | | apiDoc | yes | The site's model output path (api-doc/<namespace>.json). | | Field | Required | What it is | | ---------- | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | fidelity | no | Defaults to fidelity/<namespace>.json. A fork records no fidelity artifact (see below); the field mirrors the sibling lanes for a future hand-authored target that wants one. | | Field | Required | What it is | | ------------- | ---------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | upstreamLua | one of two | Library-folder-relative paths of the vendored upstream .lua this target's surface is measured against. See surface parity. | | Field | Required | What it is | | --------------- | ---------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | parityVerdict | one of two | Why this target vendors no upstream .lua: { "reason": ..., "note": ... }. Mutually exclusive with upstreamLua. | | Field | Required | What it is | | -------------- | ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | instanceType | when upstream has methods | The exported interface the fork declares the module's instances with, e.g. BehaviorTree. Required once the vendored upstream defines a function M:name(…) method, which parity measures against that interface's methods; it needs upstreamLua. See surface parity. | A missing required field fails loudly, naming the field, the offending entry and its library.json. So does a folder named other than its repository, a folder without reviewed.json, and a module another library folder already names. upstreamLua and parityVerdict are individually optional but jointly mandatory: every entry declares exactly one. Neither field is in the required list, yet an entry declaring neither — or both — fails the same way, naming the offender. That is deliberate. A target with no declaration would otherwise sit in the config indistinguishable from a measured-and-clean one, so the config cannot express "nobody has looked at this yet"; you either measure the surface or record why you cannot.

20147.content: Put the authored/forked declaration at the authored path. For a fork of a ts-defold binding, that is the ts-defold lane's codemodded output (codemodDeclaration in packages/cli/src/library/sync-library-types.ts) — not the raw ts-defold fixture, which the ts-defold lane type-maps on the way out (hash/url/vmath.vector3 → Hash/Url/Vector3) while the authored lane emits its input verbatim, so forking the fixture would ship upstream's Lua type names and fail the dts-declaration-validity gate. The two forms coincide when the library references no mapped core types (persist), which is why the rule is safe to state unconditionally. For a hand-authored library, it is the declaration you wrote. Either way it must be a declare module '<moduleId>' ambient — the target form the emit passes through unchanged. When the library is a native extension, the declaration also carries / @globalTable / so project imports lower to its runtime global rather than a require (see Module form). Then run this command from the toolchain root: resolve serves the vendored .d.ts with one change: each member upstream documents carries upstream's LuaDoc summary as its doc comment unless the fork's own comment is pinned to that text (see Upstream LuaDoc import). Nothing else is transformed: an authored source is already target-form, so the served types are the vendored types. --api-doc-out makes library check, once its checks pass, run extractApiDoc over that printed declaration under the pinned publish namespace, producing the api-doc/<namespace>.json the /api page renders. A member's @deprecated tag carries through to the page as a Deprecated line, with the tag's own text when it has any — so mark a deprecated member in the fork rather than only saying so in its prose. There is no fetch command — the source is vendored by hand, not snapshotted from a primary source — and no fidelity command: there is no primary source to compare against, and the emit is lossless by construction (see below).

20148.content: The generated lanes report a coverage number because a parse can lose type information the original had. An authored .d.ts cannot: the printed declaration is the vendored source plus doc comments, so the go/no-go gate is a forked-vs-printed identity diff on types — what resolve prints, with its comments removed, is identical to the vendored fork/<moduleId>.d.ts with its comments removed. sync-authored-types.test.ts asserts this for every fork, and print-library.test.ts checks the lane dispatch serves that print. No fidelity/ artifact is written. Read that gate narrowly. It proves emission fidelity — both sides of the diff are the toolchain repo's own files, so all it certifies is that the print loses no type relative to the vendored .d.ts. It says nothing about whether the vendored surface matches upstream, and there is no primary source to measure it against — that is what "no structured type source" means. A verbatim fork inherits whatever accuracy the binding it copied already had; a corrected fork (see defsave below) is only as accurate as the manual audit behind it. So pin the corrections with per-library shape assertions in packages/cli/src/library/sync-authored-types.test.ts — the closest thing this lane has to an upstream check.

20149.content: The previous section holds for types: upstream ships none, so there is nothing to measure a fork's type annotations against. It does not hold for the surface. Upstream Lua declares its member names and its parameter names in plain source, and those are comparable — a fork that never got a member, or that dropped a trailing parameter, is measurable without any type information at all.

20150.content: The upstream path is derived from moduleId: replace the dots with slashes and append .lua, so in.button is in/button.lua and richtext.richtext is richtext/richtext.lua. Fetch that path at the library's pinned ref and vendor it under the library folder's source/upstream/, at the same path it has upstream — so britzl/defold-input at in/button.lua lands at defold-input/source/upstream/in/button.lua. Vendor only the module file the target names, never the whole repository: the parity report measures only the files the target names, so any other copy is dead weight. The reader accepts two closing forms: a bare return M, and a callable module's return setmetatable(M, { … }) — on one line or spread over several, as long as it starts at column 0. It refuses a metatable carrying index, and one named by a variable whose keys it cannot see, in both cases throwing rather than parsing. A delegated member never appears at column 0, so parsing anyway would report a short surface as the whole one and raise the target's coverage for it. An indented return setmetatable(instance, { … }) inside a factory function is not the module's close and is ignored, which is what the column-0 rule buys. The reader also reads the entries of the returned table's constructor: a column-0 local M = { whose entries run over the following lines gives each top-level name = value entry as a member, a function(…) value as a callable one, so this constructor counts Client as M.Client = Client would: A constructor that closes on its opening line, local M = { NAME = "admob" }, is read too. A nested table's keys stay out. An entry it cannot name — a bracketed ["key"] or a positional value — or entries written on an opening line whose constructor continues past it throw, for the same reason a delegating metatable does. A class module's column-0 function M:name(…) methods are read as well, each with its named parameters and without the implicit self. Parity keys them <instanceType>:<name> and compares them with the methods of the interface the entry names as its instanceType, so a missing or short method costs callable coverage like any other member. The self-index M.index = M that makes the module a class adds no member. A column-0 colon method on any other table throws, since its instances are reached through nothing the reader sees, and so does a name defined both as a method and as a . member. List the vendored paths in upstreamLua, then regenerate: That writes fidelity/authored/<namespace>.json per measured target. Both halves of the upstream surface are compared, on two axes reported side by side. The declared side of each is the fork's api-doc/<namespace>.json — the surface the /api page renders, so the report measures what a reader actually sees. Only the fork's own members are compared. An api-doc element marked global: true is a file-scope name the library installs into the environment, defined upstream in files the target does not vendor, so it is a member of no module and enters neither axis — calling one a phantom would describe real upstream API as invented. declaredGlobals records how many were set aside: 30 for deftest, whose telescope assertions are ambient, and 87 for boom, which declares one module member beside its whole ambient game API. The callable axis, upstream members carrying a parameter list against api-doc FUNCTION elements: | Field | What it counts | | ----------------- | --------------------------------------------- | | upstreamMembers | Callable members the upstream module defines. | | Field | What it counts | | ----------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | declaredGlobals | Declared names the fork installs into the environment rather than onto the module. Counted, never compared. | | Field | What it counts | | ----------------- | ---------------------------- | | declaredMembers | Functions the fork declares. | | Field | What it counts | | ---------------- | -------------------------------------------------- | | missingMembers | Upstream members the fork does not declare at all. | | Field | What it counts | | ---------------- | ---------------------------------------- | | phantomMembers | Declared members upstream does not have. | | Field | What it counts | | ----------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | arityMismatches | Shared names whose parameter counts disagree, each with both numbers — the fork's being the widest signature it declares. Names are not compared — a fork may rename parameters freely. | | Field | What it counts | | --------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | undocumentedMembers | Upstream prose that reached neither the fork nor the import — a member whose accepted block carries no summary to lower, being nothing but tags or nothing but the member's own name. | | Field | What it counts | | -------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | | importedDocs | Declared elements carrying upstream's own doc, its summary or only its parameter and return docs, because the fork supplied none or did not pin its own. Counted on both axes. | | Field | What it counts | | ------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | refusedDocBlocks | Refused upstream blocks the fork left unanswered — neither documented in the fork's own words nor excused by a recorded parityException. Counted on both axes, and the one term that reports prose the import never saw. Authoring the brief clears the charge. | | Field | What it counts | | ----------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | | refusedDocBlocksTotal | The raw refusal count, before the answered and excused ones are subtracted. Kept so a refusedDocBlocks of 0 cannot be misread as upstream writing no ---only blocks. | | Field | What it counts | | ----------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | variadicMembers | Shared members compared against a floor rather than an exact count, upstream being variadic. | | Field | What it counts | | ------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | overloadedMembers | Shared members the fork declares as several overloads, so the comparison had a set of counts to accept rather than one. | | Field | What it counts | | -------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | placeholderMembers | Shared members whose upstream definition ends in a bare with no ... after it, dropped before the counts were compared. | | Field | What it counts | | ------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------- | | callableCoverage | Fraction of upstream members that are declared and agree on arity. | An upstream definition ending in ... has no fixed parameter count to disagree with, so function M.play(...) is compared against its named parameters as a floor: the fork must declare at least them, and anything beyond is the rest. variadicMembers says how many shared members that weaker check covered, so a callableCoverage of 1 over a variadic surface cannot be read as fully verified. A fork may also declare one name as several overloads, modelling an upstream body that branches on whether an argument was passed — monarch.transitions.gui.create declares create(node) and create() against upstream's single M.create(node) and its if node then branch. That is a set of call shapes, and the member agrees when any one of them meets the rule above; reading a single count would charge a correct fork for whichever overload the api-doc happened to list last. A disagreement is still reported as one number, the widest shape the fork offers. overloadedMembers counts every member compared that way, for the same reason variadicMembers exists: agreeing because one shape matched is a weaker result than agreeing outright. A generated module can also end a definition in a bare that no body reads and no doc comment describes — nakama.lua opens "Code generated by codegen/generate-rest.go" and 66 of its exports end that way. A trailing discard is not a parameter a consumer can pass meaningfully, so charging the fork for omitting it would report the instrument's defect as the fork's. It is dropped before the counts are compared, and only when it is last: a upstream names in the middle still has to be passed for the parameters after it to land. A written before a ... tail is last only in appearance — a caller fills that slot for any vararg to land — so it is still charged. placeholderMembers counts every member the drop covered, whether or not it changed the verdict. The drop is not merely subtractive — a fork that declared the discard as a real parameter disagrees once it is gone, which is how create_protobuf_any was found declaring a second parameter upstream does not take. The field axis, upstream constants (M.SOME_CONSTANT = "X") against api-doc VARIABLE elements. A TYPEDEF is a type rather than a runtime member and enters neither axis: | Field | What it counts | | ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------- | | upstreamFields | Non-callable members the upstream module defines. | | Field | What it counts | | ---------------- | --------------------------------------- | | declaredFields | Non-callable members the fork declares. | | Field | What it counts | | --------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | missingFields | Upstream constants the fork does not declare — values its users cannot reach. | | Field | What it counts | | --------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | phantomFields | Declared constants upstream has in neither half — names the fork invented. | | Field | What it counts | | --------------- | ---------------------------------------------- | | fieldCoverage | Fraction of upstream fields the fork declares. | A name that is callable on either side belongs to the callable axis and is never also counted as a field, so one defect is never charged twice. A fork that declared an upstream function as a constant of a callable type would otherwise be charged on both axes at once — once as a missing member, once as a phantom field — and the second charge would describe an upstream name as invented. No measured target produces the shape today, the one that did having since been corrected, so the rule stands on the classifier rather than on any corpus case. floors in the library's library.json ratchets both axes per module, keyed by moduleId as { "callable": 1, "field": 1 }, each against its own floor: either may rise, neither may fall. A regeneration that lowers either number reds the gate, a floor entry that names only one axis is rejected when the library is read rather than leaving the other unratcheted, and library check measures the fork against the same floors. A non-empty missingMembers, phantomMembers, arityMismatches, missingFields, or phantomFields is a correction to make in the fork — never a number to re-baseline. The measurement exists so the gap stays visible while it is being closed; the current numbers are the honest starting point, not a target. The committed reports are held to a fresh measurement for the same reason: authored-parity-floor.test.ts re-measures every target and reds when a committed report differs, so a re-vendor, fork edit or reader change that moves a number reds until bun run --cwd packages/library-types parity rewrites the reports and the coverage change is reviewed. nakama is the worked example and the rollout's closing statement: its fork declared 166 functions against upstream's 156 with only 4 agreeing on arity — the corpus's worst case, and the last target to reach a full callableCoverage. Closing it took every kind of correction this page describes. Requests upstream had flattened into positional parameters were still declared as a body table, so a caller following the fork passed a table where upstream reads a string. 84 exports ended in retry_policy, cancellation_token the fork declared nowhere, and the two types that pair with them — cancel and cancellation_token — were themselves among the 16 members it never declared. 26 declared names were not on this module at all, the realtime socket surface among them: the pinned nakama.lua requires that module privately and exposes it only through create_socket. Eleven of the 26 have a counterpart on nakama.socket, now vendored as a target of its own; the other fifteen — thirteen message constructors, a stream-presence listener and a request constructor upstream no longer generates — match neither module at the pin and were phantoms on an older nakama-defold. The field axis then closed on the same terms: all 12 of upstream's enum constants are declared, so both axes read 1. boom is the opposite shape: it declares one of the six members boom/boom.lua defines, the other five being the final/init/on_input/ on_message/update lifecycle hooks boom.script calls rather than API a user writes. Those five are justified rather than missing — see below — so the target reports callableCoverage: 1 with no fork edit at all. Read that beside declaredGlobals: nearly the whole library reaches its users as ambient globals, which this axis does not measure.

20151.content: Some divergences are not defects. When upstream's own source says a member is not for consumers, declaring it would widen the published surface with a function nobody should call — so the fork is right to omit it, and the report should say so rather than charge it as a gap. parityExceptions in the library's library.json is where that is recorded. It maps each fork's namespace to an array of { name, kind, reason } entries sorted by name. An excepted member counts as correct, is absent from missingMembers, and appears in the artifact's parityExceptions carrying its reason — so a target that reached 1 by justification reads differently from one that reached 1 by declaring everything. kind is a closed set, in the same shape as parityVerdict's reason: | kind | When it applies | | ------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | script-lifecycle | Upstream exports the member for the library's own bundled .script and says so in its own comment. boom's five hooks carry -- called from boom.script; orthographic.camera's init, final and update say "called automatically from … the camera.script" in LuaDoc. | | kind | When it applies | | ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | | deprecated-stub | Upstream's body is nothing but error("… is deprecated"), so the member cannot succeed if called. orthographic.camera keeps ten such one-line stubs; six are excepted here. | reason must cite upstream's file and line, so the entry can be re-checked against the pin instead of taken on trust. An arity or phantom exception is deliberately not expressible — no kind is added before a real case asks for one. An entry cannot outlive the defect it justifies. Three throws enforce that, each naming the offending entry: an unknown kind, rejected at parse time; an entry naming a member the pinned upstream does not define — the member was renamed or removed, and the entry is stale; an entry for a member the fork does declare — the exception is unnecessary and must be deleted rather than left to rot. The ledger is not a way to skip a correction. It is the other half of correct it or justify it, and every entry is a claim about upstream that the next reader can check.

20152.content: A measured target's printed declaration does not stop at the fork. Where upstream documents a module-level member and the fork does not override it with a pinned comment, upstream's own LuaDoc summary, parameter docs and return docs are printed as that member's doc comment, so a project's editor shows them on hover. The api-doc is lowered from the same printed declaration, so the /api page shows the same text, marked so a reader can tell it apart from the fork's own prose. Six rules bound it: Parameter and return docs follow the declared signature. The summary ends at the first line starting with @. Each @param or @tparam text prints as an @param on every declaration that lists that parameter, in the declaration's order, so an overload carries only its own; @return or @treturn text prints as @returns unless the declaration returns void, and a constant takes no tags. Types never print: a ---@param line is read as LuaLS (name type description), every other line as LDoc (name description, a (type) or a @tparam type dropped), and a following line that opens no tag continues the text. A tag with no description, a vararg ..., and a dotted table field such as config.dsn print nothing. An @ after a space, such as LDoc's @{name} reference, prints as \@ so TypeScript reads it as text rather than as a tag. One blank line inside a comment run does not end the block. Upstream often wraps a long @param list around a blank line, which would otherwise truncate the block to its tag half and lose the summary above it. The blank is crossed only when the segment touching the definition opens no --- block of its own, so a blank-separated section header above a documented member never merges into it, and only ever one blank is crossed. A brief never restates its own symbol. Where upstream writes the member's name as the block's first line and the summary beneath it, the name line is dropped, so the rendered brief is the summary rather than the symbol you are already reading. A first line that merely mentions the name is prose and survives; a block that is only the name imports nothing at all. Fork prose wins only while pinned. A member upstream documents keeps exactly what the fork wrote, on every overload, only while the fork's comment carries an @upstreamDoc pin matching upstream's current text (see Pinning a fork comment); a pinned comment replaces upstream's tags as well as its summary. Without a pin, or with a stale one, upstream's summary, parameter docs and return docs replace the fork's summary and its @param and @returns tags; every other tag, such as @noSelf or @deprecated, stays. A member upstream does not document keeps the fork's comment, pinned or not. A comment holding only tags, such as / @noSelf /, is not a summary: the print puts upstream's doc at the top of that same block, and an @param or @returns the fork wrote there keeps its slot. Only the module's own members. The merge fills the functions and constants directly inside the declare module block. A file-scope global and a member of a nested namespace keep whatever the fork wrote. The import is printed, never vendored. fork/<moduleId>.d.ts is untouched and the print changes comments only, so the identity diff on types still proves the emit is lossless, imported prose stays distinguishable from the fork's forever after, and an upstream doc change reaches the print with no hand edit. A block whose every segment opens with a plain -- rather than --- is refused, and counted as refusedDocBlocksTotal on the target's parity report. Nothing distinguishes such a block from a section header sitting above a run of constants — monarch's -- transition messages and boom's -- initialize boom are the same shape to any parser — so admitting the class would attach one member's heading to another's documentation. The remedy is to author that member's doc-comment in the fork, where a human makes the judgment and the result correctly renders as first-party. refusedDocBlocks charges only the refusals still unanswered, so the remedy actually clears it: write the brief and the member stops counting. A member the fork deliberately does not declare is excused by its parityException instead — there is no element to hang a brief on, and the ledger already carries a human's reading of that same comment, which is why boom's five lifecycle blocks charge nothing. A merely missingMembers name is not excused: its remedy is declaring it. The raw term is what keeps the refusal itself visible — defmath writes all 36 of its blocks that way and charges none of them, every one being answered in the fork's own words. An imported symbol's /api heading carries a U dot labelled Documentation imported from upstream, beside the G dot an ambient global carries. The page's provenance block already names the repo and ref the text came from.

20153.content: A fork comment on a member upstream documents is an override of upstream's text, so it names the text it replaces. Its last line is @upstreamDoc and a 12-character pin, on a line of its own: The pin is a hash of upstream's whole LuaDoc block for that member, tags included, with whitespace collapsed, so re-indenting or re-wrapping upstream's comment keeps it and changing a word or a @param line does not. The pin never prints: the line is removed from the served declaration and the /api page. library check names every fork comment that prints upstream's doc instead, with the pin that would keep it: A notice never fails the check, so an update whose upstream edits a doc you override still lands; it prints upstream's new text until you read it, then either copy the pin into the fork's comment or delete the comment when upstream now says it well. A pin on a member upstream does not document guards nothing and is named as well. A pin shaped any other way, or placed anywhere but a module function's or constant's doc comment, stops the module from printing.

20154.content: Neither number is "the" coverage of a target, and no single figure replaces them. A module can agree completely on one axis while missing the other entirely, so folding them into one mean would let each mask the other — exactly the reading the split exists to prevent. platypus is the worked case. It defines one module function and 14 constants, so its callableCoverage is 1 over a single comparison while its fieldCoverage is 1 over fourteen. Both read the same, and they are not the same result: one is a single create agreeing on arity, the other is fourteen constants each found by name. Averaged into one figure the module would look uniformly verified, and the single number would move by a fourteenth for a defect on either side — which is why the two are reported separately whether they agree or not. Read the two together. A perfect callableCoverage over a handful of functions still says nothing about a large upstreamFields, and a perfect fieldCoverage says nothing about arity. A phantom on either axis enters no coverage figure, having no upstream member to be a fraction of, so it is visible only in its list.

20155.content: Record a parityVerdict instead of an empty upstreamLua. The reason comes from a closed set — an unknown one throws, naming the entry — and the note must say what was actually looked at: | reason | When it applies | | ----------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | unresolved-path | The moduleId-derived path does not resolve at the pinned ref, including a repository that no longer exists there. No corpus target carries this verdict. Before recording it, check whether the upstream merely moved — an account rename usually redirects, and the same history may be reachable under a new owner. If it is genuinely gone, prefer dropping the library over shipping types nobody can obtain a runtime for. | | reason | When it applies | | ---------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | no-module-file | Upstream resolves, but declares no single module file this target could be measured against. | | reason | When it applies | | ------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | unparseable-shape | The module file exists but closes in a way the reader refuses — a metatable carrying index, or one it cannot read the keys of, either of which could delegate members no column-0 scan would find. No corpus target carries this verdict: boom.boom and in.accelerometer once did, and were lifted into measurement when the reader learned the return setmetatable(M, { call = … }) form they close with. | A verdict is a recorded finding, not a way to skip the work. It says someone looked and what stopped them, which is exactly what an absent declaration cannot say. The corpus currently carries no verdict of any kind — all 35 targets are measured — so every reason above is described rather than exemplified.

20156.content: Severing ts-defold for the library is the same single-module cutover the generated lanes use: Drop the library's row from library-targets.json and its dir from library-classification.json, and delete the retired fixtures/ts-defold/<moduleId>.d.ts. Its api-doc/<moduleId>.json golden is deleted only when the fork publishes under a different namespace; when namespace === moduleId it is instead overwritten in place by the command above. The namespace now resolves to your authored artifacts. Add a usage/<library>-usage.test-d.ts compile proof in the library folder, moving any hand-written block for the old dotted specifier into it. library check type-checks every .ts file under a library's usage/ under skipLibCheck: false together with every module resolve prints, the fork among them. The ts-defold registry is now empty: every library it once carried has severed, so library-targets.json holds "targets": []. The file stays committed anyway — the CLI's registry loader treats a missing file as "no vendored libraries at all" and would drop the LuaLS, script_api and authored lanes with it, and library-classification.json pins its commit against that source block. The site's fourth maintainedHere loader reads each library's forks, so the namespace becomes authored-here — absent from the ts-defold classification and present in a first-party corpus — and its /api page carries the upstream pin automatically. Then run the gates: Commit the library's library.json and reviewed.json, the vendored fork/<moduleId>.d.ts and its usage/ examples together, along with the config and manifest deletions. The emitted api-doc/ report folder is gitignored here and stays uncommitted.

20157.content: britzl/defcon is a plain-Lua console library with no .script_api and no ---@ annotations, so it is a Bucket-E authored target. Its ts-defold binding was a correct 24-line single-module surface, and the surface is small and stable — exactly the low-maintenance-cost case the fork path is for. Keeping it ts-defold-sourced would forgo the provenance gain for no real saving; a fresh hand-author would be redundant work when the existing binding is already right. So the decision is fork: copy the retired .d.ts verbatim, sever ts-defold, and pin to the real upstream. The reference defcon/library.json: and defcon/reviewed.json pins { "ref": "2.6.0" }. authored vendors the fork; moduleId defcon.console names the declare module a consumer imports; namespace defcon is the single-segment artifact stem, so the golden is api-doc/defcon.json — not the dotted moduleId — keeping the docs Libraries tree and file layout uniform with the other bare-stem severed libraries. Nothing else owned defcon, so it was free to take; orthographic.camera below is the case where it is not. The defcon page then attributes to britzl/defcon at 2.6.0, not the ts-defold/library corpus.

20158.content: britzl/deftest (a test runner, pinned to 2.8.0) is a second fork with the same reference-entry shape as defcon.console. It illustrates one wrinkle: its .d.ts declares ambient top-level globals (describe, before, after, test, assert) alongside declare module 'deftest.deftest'. A fork copies the surface verbatim, so those globals carry into the printed declaration and therefore into the dts-declaration-validity gate's compilation. That is fine — they raise no duplicate-identifier clash — and the api-doc lowering publishes them alongside the module's exports (add, run), each marked as an ambient global so the reference page distinguishes what the import reaches from what is callable without it. Do not alter a vendored fork to suppress such globals; they are part of the library's real surface. A file-scope type is held to a stricter rule than a file-scope value: it publishes only when a published signature names it and it carries members (an interface, or a type alias over an object literal). A union, a function type, or an internal generic helper stays off the page, so a fork's incidental type machinery does not become reference content.

20159.content: subsoap/defmath (a pure-Lua math-helper module) is a third fork with the same reference-entry shape, illustrating the no-tag case: upstream publishes no git tags, so ref pins the default-branch commit SHA (c67c227322334056cea7a631f3ddcdf2bcfd480c) rather than a semver tag. The defmath page attributes to that SHA and its sourceUrl points at .../tree/c67c2273… — expected, not a defect. Its surface also references core engine types: upstream writes them as vmath.vector3 | vmath.vector4 / vmath.quaternion, but the fork — like every vendored declaration in this package — carries the core-type-renamed ambient Vector3 | Vector4 / Quaternion. These resolve in library check, which compiles every fork against the engine types the CLI ships, so a fork consuming engine types needs no special wiring.

20160.content: subsoap/defsave (a save/load helper, pinned to the v1.2.6 tag) is the first fork to correct a surface rather than re-home it: the ts-defold binding declared 7 of upstream's 14 functions and just one of its 16 config fields (appname), and three of the seven returned the wrong type. Neither pure option fits — keep fails the cost model (upstream is frozen and the surface is tiny) and a fork alone would knowingly re-home a half-missing surface, while a full hand-author would rewrite five declarations that are already right (four correct functions plus appname). So fork first, then hand-correct against the pin: copy the retired .d.ts, add the missing members, and fix the wrong signatures reading upstream's Lua as the authority. Extending a fork is gate-safe: the identity diff compares the printed declaration to the vendored fixture, not to the retired ts-defold surface. But that diff proves emission fidelity only — the print loses nothing relative to the vendored .d.ts; it does not check the vendored surface against upstream. That accuracy rests on the manual audit against defsave.lua at the pin plus the per-library shape assertions in packages/cli/src/library/sync-authored-types.test.ts, so correcting a fork moves the accuracy burden onto the author, not onto a gate. Narrowing a wrong return is a breaking change for consumers and belongs in the changelog's ### Breaking section; a types package's value is accuracy, so do not keep a declaration you can see is wrong. Two limits are worth knowing before you correct a surface. Upstream Lua that falls off the end of a function returns nil, so a predicate like defsave's key_exists is boolean | undefined, not boolean — read every branch, not just the explicit returns. And a module's export let fields are still read-only through a consumer's import as ns, so a compile proof pins their types by reading them; there is no way to prove assignability through a namespace import.

20161.content: whiteboxdev/library-defold-persist (a save/load helper, pinned to the b37f6104… commit SHA since upstream publishes no tags) is the first fork to arrive here from a markdown no-go rather than from having no documented source at all. Its README documents all six functions by name but no parameters and no returns, so the markdown gate scored signature-loss and refused the cutover. That verdict retired the README as a regeneration path — and nothing more. Running the cost model on the still-open maintenance question gives fork: the ts-defold surface is five fully-typed functions in 34 lines, upstream is abandoned (its README redirects to a successor project) so the surface cannot churn, and the recorded loss was the README's, not the .d.ts's. So the cutover itself was verbatim — the identity diff made fidelity 100% by construction, and it shipped no type change at all. The later and separately-auditable edit that anticipated has since landed: the fork now also declares exists, the sixth function upstream's Lua defines and ts-defold never had. Severing does not erase the markdown verdict. persist's no-go/signature-loss record and its README snapshot stay exactly as recorded, and the gate still re-derives the decision on every run — it just compares against the vendored fork instead of the deleted fixtures/ts-defold/ snapshot. That is sound because the comparison is re-derived against whatever the fork now declares, not against an identity: adding exists moved two name-set terms and left the no-go/signature-loss decision exactly where it was. Keeping a dead library-targets.json row alive to feed that lookup would have been the wrong fix: it would make the file stop meaning still ts-defold-sourced, which is the signal the remaining Bucket-C libraries are measured against.

20162.content: britzl/defold-orthographic (a camera suite, pinned to tag 3.6.3) is a second markdown no-go that answered fork, and it settles two questions persist's surface never raised.
